target.title: fix(gateway): avoid duplicate launchd restart bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway restart` can create a second gateway on macOS installs where the gateway is managed by a user LaunchAgent with `RunAtLoad`/`KeepAlive`.

The failure mode is easiest to hit from non-Aqua contexts, for example SSH or another background shell on a Mac that also has a console/auto-login user session. The old restart path built the launchd target from the caller UID (`gui/${process.getuid()}`), then ran `launchctl kickstart -k`. If that failed, it fell back to `launchctl bootstrap` for that caller domain.

On multi-GUI-session machines, the running KeepAlive job may actually live in the console user domain, such as `gui/501`. Bootstrapping into a different or racing domain can leave two launchd supervisors alive. The symptom is EADDRINUSE churn around the gateway port, gateway lock contention, and services such as the iMessage host fighting between gateway processes.

## Repro Shape

1. macOS gateway installed as a user LaunchAgent with `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive`.
2. The active gateway is supervised in the console/auto-login GUI domain.
3. Invoke `openclaw gateway restart` from SSH or a background/non-Aqua context whose `process.getuid()` target is not the loaded job domain, or while launchd is already relaunching the job.
4. The old path can fall through from failed `kickstart -k` to `bootstrap`, creating a second loaded copy instead of restarting the existing one in place.

## Fix

- Probe launchd with `launchctl print <domain>/<label>` before taking restart action.
- Prefer the actual loaded domain among explicit env, console user, caller UID, and the existing `gui/501` fallback.
- Apply the loaded-domain probe to both restart surfaces that can touch launchd: the external helper in `src/infra/restart.ts` and the actual CLI service restart owner path in `src/daemon/launchd.ts`.
- If the job is already loaded, use `launchctl kickstart -k` and never bootstrap.
- Bootstrap only after `launchctl print` confirms the job is not loaded.
- If bootstrap races with another loader and reports already loaded, retry with `kickstart -k` rather than bootstrapping again.
- Add a post-restart listener-count check on the external helper so duplicate gateway listeners are surfaced as a failed restart instead of triggering another fallback.

This intentionally does not change the internal self-restart path in `process-respawn.ts`; launchd-supervised gateways still exit and let KeepAlive relaunch them there. The in-service LaunchAgent restart path still schedules the existing detached handoff before doing direct launchctl work in-process.

## Evidence

- External helper regression coverage models a loaded launchd job and asserts `triggerOpenClawRestart` runs `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway` followed by `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, with no `bootstrap` call.
- CLI owner-path regression coverage now models `openclaw gateway restart` resolving a loaded console LaunchAgent after a caller-domain miss: `launchctl print gui/777/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl enable gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, with no `bootstrap` or `bootout` call.
- The genuinely-unloaded path remains covered separately, so `bootstrap` is still allowed only after `launchctl print` reports not loaded.
- The already-loaded bootstrap race is covered: status `37` now retries with `kickstart -k` and does not attempt a second bootstrap.
- Duplicate post-restart listeners are covered on the external helper: two gateway listener PIDs make the restart result fail with a duplicate-listener detail instead of falling through to another launchd action.
- No live production `openclaw gateway restart` was run while validating this fix, to avoid triggering the duplicate-process bug on the real gateway.

### Live macOS LaunchAgent proof (2026-07-01)

- Ran PR head `fd92beecad95f6a3a0a8a935113db38192d35d9f` on a real macOS user LaunchAgent using a disposable label, `ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof`, in `gui/501`.
- The disposable job was already loaded before invoking the PR restart helper: `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof` returned `state = running`, `runs = 1`, `pid = 58095`.
- Invoked `triggerOpenClawRestart()` with `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL=ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof`, `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_DOMAIN=gui/501`, and an unused temp gateway port. It returned:
  ```json
  {"ok":true,"method":"launchctl","tried":["launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof","launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof"]}
  ```
- No `launchctl bootstrap` was attempted for the already-loaded job.
- After restart, `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof` returned `state = running`, `runs = 2`, `pid = 58131`, `last exit code = 0`; the proof worker events showed start -> SIGTERM -> start.
- Production gateway listener on `18789` was unchanged before/after the proof run, and cleanup booted out the disposable LaunchAgent successfully.

## Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/service.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts src/daemon/launchd.ts src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts src/daemon/service.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts src/daemon/launchd.ts src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts src/daemon/service.test.ts`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`

target.title: fix(mcp): allow SecretRef values in mcp.servers env and headers [AI-assisted]
target.body:
## Summary

This PR adds SecretRef support to core MCP server configuration so `mcp.servers.*.env.*` and `mcp.servers.*.headers.*` can use SecretInput values in addition to plaintext literals.

Before this change, core `mcp.servers` only accepted primitive literal values on these surfaces, which meant MCP credentials on the built-in config path had to remain plaintext even though other SecretRef-capable surfaces already supported resolved runtime credentials.

## What changed

- allow `SecretInput` values in `mcp.servers.*.env.*`
- allow `SecretInput` values in `mcp.servers.*.headers.*`
- include core MCP env/header targets in command/runtime secret resolution
- resolve only the active MCP transport surface at runtime
- include core MCP env/header targets in the supported SecretRef target registry
- teach `secrets configure` and `secrets audit` to handle MCP env/header targets without promoting generic non-secret literals like URLs and feature flags
- update the MCP and SecretRef docs/matrix to document the supported surface

## Why

This keeps sensitive MCP credentials out of plaintext config while preserving the existing runtime model:

- config stores SecretRefs
- activation resolves active refs into the in-memory runtime snapshot
- spawned MCP processes receive resolved string values at launch time

That is consistent with the rest of OpenClaw’s SecretRef model and removes a real gap on the core `mcp.servers` surface.

## Validation

Passed locally:

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm check`

Passed targeted coverage for the touched surface:

- `src/config/config-misc.test.ts`
- `src/secrets/configure-plan.test.ts`
- `src/secrets/target-registry.docs.test.ts`
- `src/secrets/runtime-core-snapshots.test.ts`

- `src/commands/agent.runtime-config.test.ts`

Additional functional validation:

- verified a core stdio MCP server configured through `mcp.servers.*.env.*` receives resolved string env values at launch time while the config itself still stores SecretRef objects
- verified custom credential-like names such as `SERVICE_KEY` and `X-Access-Key` are treated as sensitive by configure/audit flows
- verified generic literals such as URLs and feature-flag headers are not promoted as secret targets

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: `mcp.servers.*.env.*` and `mcp.servers.*.headers.*` only accepted primitive string literals before this PR. Passing a SecretRef object (`{"source":"env","id":"MC_API_KEY"}`) as an MCP env or header value caused `config validate` to return `Invalid input`. target.title: feat(doctor): detect local rebuild vs pristine npm release
target.body:
## Problem

A stock `openclaw update` silently overwrites locally patched installs.
Regressions return quietly because operators have no signal that the
running package has diverged from the pristine npm release.

Concrete trigger: the 2026-04-20 dist-overlay audit of
`/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw` on a production host showed
v2026.4.15 with `dist/build-info.json.builtAt = 2026-04-19` while the
npm registry reported that version was published on `2026-04-16`.
That ~3-day skew is a locally rebuilt install — a stock `update` had
wiped a sticky-fallback patch that had been applied by hand.

## Solution

Non-blocking `openclaw doctor` note that compares local build metadata
against the npm registry publish time and warns if the installed
package is a local rebuild, an unreleased version, or has corrupt
metadata.

* **Warn only.** Never fails doctor.
* **Silent on pristine or inconclusive** (no network, no cache, etc.).
* **Runs in the install-posture section** of `doctor`, right after
  `noteSourceInstallIssues`.

## Signals

* Reads `<packageRoot>/dist/build-info.json` → `{version, commit, builtAt}`
  and `<packageRoot>/package.json.version`.
* Fetches `https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw`, inspects
  `.time[<version>]`.
* **rebuild** — `builtAt - publishedAt >= 60 min`.
* **unreleased** — version not present in registry `.time`.
* **corrupt** — local `build-info.json` / `package.json` missing or
  malformed.
* **inconclusive** — registry fetch failed and no usable cache
  (silent, to avoid false positives on air-gapped installs).
* **pristine** — otherwise.

Registry response cached at `~/.openclaw/rebuild-guard-cache.json`
with a 6h TTL. Honors `OPENCLAW_NPM_REGISTRY_FILE` for tests and an
`offline: true` option for environments that should never hit the
network.

## Test coverage

`src/commands/doctor-rebuild-guard.test.ts` (8/8 green):

* pristine within the skew window
* rebuild when `builtAt` is >= 60 min after npm publish
* unreleased (version not in registry)
* corrupt (missing / malformed `build-info.json`)
* inconclusive (fetch throws, no cache) → silent
* offline mode (no network call, decides from local only)
* cache hit (second call, within TTL, does not call `fetch`)
* `noteRebuildGuardHealth` emission matrix: emits for
  `rebuild` / `unreleased` / `corrupt`; silent for
  `pristine` / `inconclusive`

## Gates

* `pnpm lint` — pass
* `pnpm tsgo:all` (typecheck) — pass
* `pnpm build` — pass
* `pnpm exec vitest run src/commands/doctor-rebuild-guard.test.ts` — 8/8

## Sample doctor output (rebuilt host)

```
└ Install ────────────────────────────────────────
  Local OpenClaw install differs from the pristine npm release.
  - Install: /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw
  - Version: 2026.4.15
  - Commit: 8abd1fc
  - builtAt: 2026-04-19T08:42:11Z
  - npm publish: 2026-04-16T19:03:47Z
  - Skew: 4197 minutes ahead of npm
  - Reason: rebuild-after-publish
  Confirm every local patch has a matching upstream PR before running `openclaw update`.
```

## Related

A companion **Layer-1 bash guard** already ships in operator
workspaces (installed as a systemd `ExecStartPre`) to surface the same
warning on daemon start. This PR makes the same check native to every
`openclaw` install so end users benefit from it too, not just
operators who maintain local workspaces.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): Add group admin privacy controls
target.body:
Closes #69233

## What changed

This adds an optional per-group WhatsApp admin override via `channels.whatsapp.groups.<jid>.admin` and wildcard `channels.whatsapp.groups."*".admin`.

When an admin is configured for a group scope:
- the configured E.164 number bypasses mention gating for that group
- non-admin group members cannot run slash commands in that group
- the configured admin remains able to run slash commands for that group

When no admin is configured, the existing group command authorization behavior is preserved.

## Why

The issue described a privacy gap in mixed-trust WhatsApp groups: non-admin members could still probe bot behavior through mentions and slash commands. The first pass of this feature covered the basic config and enforcement, but upstream readiness also needed the behavior pinned down for wildcard group config and for the no-admin-configured fallback path.

## User impact

Users can now designate a WhatsApp group admin by phone number and use that as a privacy boundary for command discovery in group chats.

This is intentionally backwards-compatible:
- groups without `admin` continue using the existing command authorization rules

target.title: add option for MCP apps support
target.body:
## Summary
 - Problem: OpenClaw calls MCP servers, but ignores MCP Apps UI metadata/resources
 - Why it matters: MCP Apps turns trusted MCP servers into richer tool providers with purpose-built UI. Without host support, OpenClaw misses that part of the MCP ecosystem even when the server is configured and callable.
- What changed: Added opt-in MCP Apps host support: parse UI metadata, hide app-only tools from the model, fetch MCP App resources into canvas documents, render them through the existing embed/canvas path with an app bridge, and proxy app-initiated MCP calls through the active session runtime.
- What changed: Added restart/reload hardening for restored app views, wider assistant canvas layout, docs, config schema support,tests, and a security-audit warning when `mcp.apps.enabled=true`.
-  What did NOT change (scope boundary): Normal MCP tool execution still works without MCP Apps. MCP Apps are default-off behind `mcp.apps.enabled`; this does not add a marketplace, new MCP server examples, or plugin-only architecture.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)
- MCP app-only tools are not materialized for the model.
- MCP Apps UI payloads are only fetched/rendered when `mcp.apps.enabled=true`.
- App bridge calls are rejected when MCP Apps are disabled.
- App bridge calls enforce app-callable tool visibility.
- Persisted/restored app views can recreate an MCP runtime after gateway restart.
- Existing `[embed]` canvas rendering remains the fallback path when MCP Apps metadata is absent or disabled.

- Target test or file:
  - New opt-in config: `mcp.apps.enabled`.
  - Default behavior is unchanged for normal MCP tools; MCP Apps UI rendering is disabled by default.
  - When enabled, trusted MCP servers can render interactive app views in chat using the existing canvas/embed path.
  - MCP Apps views may call app-visible MCP tools through the active session runtime.
  - App-only MCP tools are hidden from the model.
  - `openclaw security audit` now warns when MCP Apps are enabled.
  - Docs now describe MCP Apps setup, scope, and security considerations. 
- Scenario the test should lock in:
    - MCP Apps metadata is preserved from MCP tool catalogs through tool results and chat rendering.
    - App-only tools are hidden from the model.
    - Model-only tools are blocked from app bridge calls.
    - MCP Apps UI rendering and bridge proxy calls require `mcp.apps.enabled=true`.
    - Restored app views can recreate an MCP runtime after gateway restart.
    - Existing canvas/embed rendering remains the fallback when MCP Apps are disabled or metadata is absent.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:
    - The feature crosses runtime materialization, gateway proxying, config/bootstrap, and UI rendering. Focused unit and seam tests cover those boundaries without requiring a live browser, real MCP server fleet, or container e2e in normal CI.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any):
    - Existing canvas/embed tests covered generic iframe rendering, but not MCP Apps metadata, app-only visibility, app bridge calls, or restored MCP runtime behavior.

  ## User-visible / Behavior Changes
  - New opt-in config: `mcp.apps.enabled`.
  - Default behavior is unchanged for normal MCP tools; MCP Apps UI rendering is disabled by default.
  - When enabled, trusted MCP servers can render interactive app views in chat using the existing canvas/embed path.
  - MCP Apps views may call app-visible MCP tools through the active session runtime.
  - App-only MCP tools are hidden from the model.
  - `openclaw security audit` now warns when MCP Apps are enabled.
  - Docs now describe MCP Apps setup, scope, and security considerations.
  
## Diagram (if applicable)

  ```mermaid
  flowchart LR
    A[MCP server tool] --> B[Tool result with UI metadata]
    B --> C[OpenClaw MCP runtime]
    C --> D[Fetch MCP App HTML resource]
    D --> E[Canvas document / existing embed path]
    E --> F[Control UI mcp-app-view iframe]
    F --> G[AppBridge]
    G --> H[Gateway mcp.* proxy]
    H --> C
  ```
## Security Impact (required)
  - New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`): Yes
  - Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No
  - New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): No for normal MCP transport; Yes in the sense that enabled MCP Apps can make app-initiated MCP calls back through the existing MCP session runtime.
  - Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`): Yes
  - Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`): Yes
  - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
    - Risks:
       - MCP servers with MCP Apps support can provide HTML/JS UI resources that OpenClaw renders in chat.
       -  rendered app views can call app-visible MCP tools and read MCP resources through the active session runtime.
       - app views receive the tool input/result payload they are rendering.
    - Mitigations:
        - MCP Apps are default-off behind `mcp.apps.enabled=true`.
        - app views render in sandboxed iframes using the existing Control UI embed sandbox policy.
        - app-only tools are hidden from the model, and model-only tools are blocked from app bridge calls.
        - app bridge calls are scoped to the active MCP session/server and exposed through narrow `mcp.*` gateway methods.
        - `openclaw security audit` warns when MCP Apps are enabled.
- Trust model: enabling MCP Apps means trusting the configured MCP servers not only as tool providers, but also as UI code providers.

  ## Repro + Verification

  ### Environment
  - OS: macOS
  - Runtime/container: local OpenClaw container via Podman
  - Model/provider: Claude Sonnet 4.6
  - Integration/channel (if any): Control UI chat with configured MCP servers
  - Relevant config (redacted):

```json
  {
    "mcp": {
      "apps": {
        "enabled": true
      },
      "servers": {
        "system-monitor": {
          "command": "npx",
          "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-system-monitor", "--stdio"]
        },
        "pdf": {
          "command": "npx",
          "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-pdf", "--stdio"]
        },
        "qr": {
          "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3108/mcp",
          "transport": "streamable-http"
        }
      }
    }
  }
```

### Steps
  1. Build and run an OpenClaw image from this branch.
  2. Enable MCP Apps with openclaw config set mcp.apps.enabled true --strict-json.
  3. Configure the system-monitor, pdf, and qr MCP servers.
  4. Start the QR MCP sidecar if using the QR example.
  5. Start a fresh chat/session in the Control UI.
  6. Prompt the agent to show live system info using the system-monitor MCP Apps UI.
  7. Prompt the agent to generate a QR code using the QR MCP Apps UI.
  8. Prompt the agent to display https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762 using the PDF MCP Apps UI.
  9. Restart the OpenClaw container and reload the Control UI.
  10. Confirm the persisted PDF app view reloads and reconnects.

### Expected

  - Normal MCP tools still work.
  - With mcp.apps.enabled=true, MCP Apps UI resources render as interactive embedded app views.
  - System monitor renders a live monitor UI.
  - QR renders an embedded QR UI.
  - PDF renders an interactive PDF viewer.
  - Restored app views can reconnect after gateway/container restart.
  - With mcp.apps.enabled=false, app bridge calls are rejected and MCP Apps render through the normal fallback path instead of the app bridge.

### Actual

  - Verified locally with system-monitor, QR, and PDF MCP Apps examples.
  - Verified upstream image comparison: upstream can call the MCP servers but does not render the MCP Apps UI resources.
  - Verified restart/reload behavior for the PDF app view.

Attach at least one:

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aaa93975-4406-493e-a060-4ac64763704b

## Review Conversations

- [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:
    - No migration is required for existing installs. MCP Apps support is default-off.
    - To enable it, set:
      ```bash
      openclaw config set mcp.apps.enabled true --strict-json
      ```
    - Configure MCP servers that expose MCP Apps / `mcp-ui` resources.
    - Restart OpenClaw so the updated config is loaded.

## Risks and Mitigations

  - Risk: Enabling MCP Apps allows configured MCP servers to provide HTML/JS UI that renders inside OpenClaw.
    - Mitigation: Feature is opt-in via `mcp.apps.enabled`; app UI renders in a sandboxed iframe; docs and security audit call out the trust boundary.
  - Risk: App views can call app-visible MCP tools/resources through the bridge, increasing the practical surface area of a trusted MCP server.
    - Mitigation: Bridge is scoped to MCP app methods only; model-only tools are blocked from app bridge calls; app-only tools are hidden from the model.
  - Risk: Restored chat views may need to reconnect to MCP runtimes after a container restart.
    - Mitigation: Gateway proxy lazily recreates the session MCP runtime from config when an app bridge call arrives and no runtime is currently active.
  - Risk: Servers without MCP Apps support, or installs with the feature disabled, should not regress.
    - Mitigation: Existing MCP tool execution path remains unchanged; UI falls back to the existing embed/canvas rendering behavior when MCP Apps are disabled or metadata is absent.

target.title: fix(gateway): prefer current route delivery context
target.body:
## Summary

- Fixes gateway agent delivery resolution so a concrete current request route (`channel`, `to`, `accountId`, `threadId`) wins over stale persisted session `deliveryContext` fields when the channels conflict.
- Clears stale route fields on channel switches when the new request does not provide replacement `to`/`accountId`/`threadId` values, avoiding mixed-channel routes.
- Preserves existing session-route behavior for normal follow-ups, `channel=last`, and same-channel existing-session routes.
- Compares same-channel targets through the channel parser so equivalent encodings do not clear stored threads.
- Populates `runContext.currentChannelId` from the resolved delivery target so downstream message-tool fallback inference sees the active route.
- Adds regression tests for the #68378 shape, channel-only stale-route clearing, same-channel partial updates, and canonical equivalent targets.

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #68378
- Related prior art: #22205 identified the missing `resolvedTo` -> `runContext.currentChannelId` propagation, but that PR is closed unmerged and does not address stale delivery-context precedence.
- Related but not duplicates: #45514, #65847, #33619, #39557, #51812, #52204 all describe adjacent multi-channel/stale-routing problems or other delivery paths; none is an open satisfactory PR for this gateway agent route-precedence bug.

## Root Cause / Diagnosis

`src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts` built `requestDeliveryHint` from the active gateway request, but then merged it with the stored session `deliveryContext` in a way that made persisted fields authoritative. That let stale persisted fields, such as Feishu `channel`/`to`, override a current Discord request before the agent command and session update were assembled. The same path also did not pass the resolved target into `runContext.currentChannelId`, so tool fallback routing could miss the current route even when `resolvedTo` was known.

A second edge case appears when the request changes only `channel`: route-field fallback must not pair a new channel with stale `lastTo`/`lastAccountId`/`lastThreadId` from the old channel.

A third edge case appears when the request and session refer to the same target with different channel-owned encodings, such as Slack `C1` and `channel:C1`: raw string comparison can falsely treat that as a target change and clear the stored thread.

## Fix

- Detect when a concrete request channel conflicts with the stored session delivery channel.
- In that cross-channel conflict case, let the current request delivery hint win and use persisted delivery metadata only as fallback for fields provided by the current route.
- Clear stale last-route fields when the current channel conflicts and no replacement field is available.
- For same-channel route conflicts, preserve unchanged target/account/thread fields unless the concrete target itself changes.
- Compare request/session targets using the channel parser before treating `to` as a target change, preserving stored threads for equivalent target spellings.
- For non-conflict cases, keep existing session delivery precedence so `channel=last`, normal follow-ups, and existing subagent routes behave as before.
- Pass `resolvedTo` into `runContext.currentChannelId` alongside the existing channel/account/thread context.
- Lock the behavior with regression tests that start from stale Feishu metadata, assert Discord wins or stale route fields are cleared, preserve partial same-channel updates, and keep Slack threads when `C1` and `channel:C1` are equivalent.

## Duplicate Sweep

Searched GitHub issues/PRs for combinations of `#68378`, Discord/Feishu wrong-channel delivery, stale `deliveryContext`, gateway agent delivery, `currentChannelId`, and multi-channel session routing. Closest results:

- #22205: overlapping `currentChannelId` propagation only; closed unmerged; no stale context precedence fix or regression for #68378.
- #35451: broader `chat.send`/cron canonical route derivation; closed unmerged; different call sites.
- #67508: target-agent bound account propagation for Matrix subagent spawns; adjacent account routing, different bug.
- #45514, #65847, #33619, #39557, #51812, #52204: related issue reports/bug class, not acceptable duplicate PRs for this exact gateway agent request-route overwrite.

Conclusion: no duplicate or already-satisfactory PR found for #68378.

## Attribution

- Thanks @Suidge for the #68378 report and follow-up logs that isolated Discord input being delivered through Feishu outbound.
- Thanks @Galygious for prior analysis in #22205 around forwarding `resolvedTo` into `runContext.currentChannelId`; this PR incorporates that same missing-context piece and adds the route-precedence fix needed for #68378.

## Testing

Fresh `origin/main` base: `64089fd15ed4ba8296612b1a622d11b5662c8b96`

- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts -t "uses the current request route"`
- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts`
- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts -t "preserves the stored thread when the request target is canonically equivalent"`
- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-a.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-b.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent.subagent-delivery-context.test.ts`

The final command covers the CI shard failures observed after the first draft and now passes locally with 71 tests.

Scoped lint note: `pnpm lint -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` is currently blocked before linting these files by the existing `src/agents/skills/*` plugin SDK boundary type errors already present on `origin/main`.

## Review Follow-up

- Addressed and resolved Codex review thread about clearing stale route fields on channel-switch merges in `5825aede6c7568f8cec2af2653d4851bf3296d78`.
- Addressed and resolved Codex review thread about preserving unchanged same-channel route fields in `d8f4d09a343f30d82df2bdeea9541a707923a72d`.
- Addressed and resolved Codex review thread about canonical target comparison in `af7506771a0fd734024ecc2b51b23b7945f27b21`.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

The change narrows routing behavior to prefer the active request route only when it conflicts with stale persisted delivery metadata, and preserves stored thread context for equivalent same-channel target spellings.

target.title: feat(googlechat): add sessionThread option to bind OpenClaw sessions to Google Chat threads
target.body: AI-assisted: yes (Claude Opus 4.7). ## Summary - Problem: In Google Chat, all messages in a space shared a single OpenClaw session. Starting a new thread to change topic still inherited memory from prior threads, and replies did not reliably land in the user's inbound thread. - Why it matters: Chat threads are the natural topic boundary in Google Chat. Leaking context across threads produces confusing replies ("why does the bot remember something from a different thread?"), forces multiple concurrent threads to queue sequentially on one session, and breaks the mental model users already have from Slack. Requested in #13373. - What changed: Added an opt-in `sessionThread` channel option. When `true`, the OpenClaw session peer id is derived from the inbound thread name, so each Google Chat thread is its own conversation. Replies are now threaded via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so bot responses land in the user's thread. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): Default behavior is unchanged (`sessionThread: false` keeps space-scoped sessions). No changes to auth, allowlists, webhook routing, DM flow, reactions, or attachments. No slash commands / `/focus`-style bindings added (see "future work" below). ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #13373 (per-thread session mode feature request) - Closes #41788 (Google Chat replies creating new threads instead of staying in the existing one) - Related #44347 — resolves the first of the two requests in that issue - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ### Note on naming vs the issue's proposal The issue proposes `threadSessionMode: "per-thread" | "per-space"`. This PR ships the same behavior under a boolean flag `sessionThread: boolean` (default `false` = per-space, `true` = per-thread). Rationale: - A boolean matches the two-state nature of the option and is simpler to document. - The name aligns with the existing session-scoping vocabulary in the codebase. - Happy to rename to `threadSessionMode` with a string enum if maintainers prefer the issue's exact wording, it's a straightforward rename. ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: The Google Chat channel used the space id as the session peer id and did not pass the inbound thread name back on outbound messages. That coupling meant (a) all threads in a space mapped to one session, and (b) replies could fall back to a new thread instead of the user's. - Missing detection / guardrail: No peer-id unit coverage for Google Chat; Slack already has `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` as prior art for this exact pattern, but nothing equivalent existed for Google Chat. - Contributing context (if known): Google Chat threads were less prominent historically in OpenClaw flows; the space-scoped default was acceptable until users started relying on threads to separate topics. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [ ] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: `resolveGoogleChatPeerId` returns the thread name when `sessionThread` is enabled and an inbound thread is present; falls back to `spaceId` otherwise; and produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions do not cross. - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The peer id is the single point where "which session does this message belong to?" is decided for Google Chat. Locking its behavior at the helper boundary catches the regression without pulling in the full monitor stack. - Existing test that already covers this (if any): None for Google Chat. Slack's `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` covers the analogous primitive. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - New opt-in config: `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` (default `false`). - `false` (default): space-scoped sessions, prior behavior unchanged. - `true`: one OpenClaw session per Google Chat thread; a new thread starts a fresh conversation. - Outbound messages now consistently target the inbound thread via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so replies land in the user's thread more reliably. This applies regardless of `sessionThread`. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text sessionThread: false (default, unchanged) space S, thread A -> session(peer=S) space S, thread B -> session(peer=S) # shared memory sessionThread: true space S, thread A -> session(peer=A) space S, thread B -> session(peer=B) # isolated memory space S, no thread -> session(peer=S) # falls back to space-scoped ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? No - Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - New/changed network calls? No (same Chat API endpoints; only request payload now sets `thread.name` and `messageReplyOption`) - Command/tool execution surface changed? No - Data access scope changed? No (in fact, `sessionThread: true` narrows memory scope per thread) ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: Node 22 / local gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway restart`) - Model/provider: any (provider-agnostic) - Integration/channel (if any): Google Chat - Relevant config (redacted): ```jsonc { "channels": { "googlechat": { "enabled": true, "serviceAccountFile": "/path/to/service-account.json", "sessionThread": true } } } ``` ### Steps 1. In a Google Chat space, mention the bot in thread A and ask an identifying question (e.g. "remember the color red"). 2. Start a new thread B in the same space and ask "what color did I mention?". 3. Reply again inside thread A and ask the same question. ### Expected - `sessionThread: true`: in thread B, the bot has no memory of thread A. In thread A, the bot still remembers "red". Replies land in the thread the user messaged in. - `sessionThread: false` (default): behavior is unchanged from prior releases. ### Actual - Matches expected for both modes. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after ``` pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is disabled ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is undefined (default) ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns thread name when sessionThread is enabled and inbound has a thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId falls back to spaceId when sessionThread is enabled but inbound has no thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions don't cross Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 5 passed (5) ``` - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - When disabled(previous behavior): - When enabled: - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) - Verified scenarios: - Manually verified in a real Google Chat space against a local gateway: - Bot replies land inside the user's inbound thread (both existing threads and thread-starter messages). - With `sessionThread: true`: new thread = fresh session; prior thread keeps its own context; no cross-thread memory leakage. - With `sessionThread: false`: unchanged, space-scoped memory. - Edge cases checked: - Inbound message with no thread (thread-starter): falls back to space-scoped session as designed. - Two concurrent threads in the same space maintain separate sessions. - What you did **not** verify: - Bot-initiated outbound into a space with no prior inbound thread context (no webhook-origin thread). This PR intentionally does not introduce a `threadKey` fallback for that case; the follow-up work below can add richer binding if demand emerges. - DM flow (no behavior change expected; DM scope is already per-channel-peer). ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? Yes - Config/env changes? Yes, additive only: new optional `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` boolean (default `false`). - Migration needed? No. Existing configs continue to behave as before. - If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A. target.title: fix(acp): treat missing cwd as stale bound session
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: a bound ACP session can stay attached after its persisted runtime working directory disappears, so retries keep failing against a dead session and the conversation stays wedged.
- Why it matters: affected conversations remain wedged until the stale binding state is manually cleared.
- What changed: during ACP dispatch, treat a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` as stale when the bound session's persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd` can no longer be resolved on disk (`ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`), then unbind the dead conversation. The signal is folded into the existing `isStaleSessionInitError` classifier and the existing `maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations` dispatch helper — no new module, no parallel helper.
- Scope: dispatch-only. Two files: `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` and its test.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- ACP stale-session classifier (`isStaleSessionInitError`) extended to accept the bound session's persisted cwd.
- Auto-reply ACP dispatch stale-binding cleanup (`maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations`) passes the persisted cwd at the `runTurn` catch.
- Regression tests: generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` + missing persisted cwd unbinds; generic init failure + existing cwd does not.

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #60720
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

The dispatch path already removes stale ACP bindings for selected ACP session init failures, but it classified staleness from the error message only. The live missing-cwd case surfaces as a generic spawn `ENOENT` wrapped as `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`, whose message does not match the stale-message set. The reliable signal is the bound session's persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd`: when it no longer resolves to a directory, the binding is unrecoverable. Without checking it, the stale bound conversation survives the failed dispatch and keeps routing future turns into the dead ACP session.

## Implementation Notes

- Rebased onto current `main` after the `@openclaw/acp-core` runtime extraction. The fix now extends `main`'s existing in-file `maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations`/`isStaleSessionInitError` instead of introducing a separate `src/acp/runtime/stale-session.ts` helper (which no longer fits the post-extraction layout). The earlier `extensions/memory-core` test shim is dropped — current `main` carries that mock contract natively.
- Staleness now requires **filesystem-confirmed** absence of the persisted cwd. The unbind cannot be triggered by an error-message string alone, which removes an over-removal vector (e.g. a transient tool error whose text mentions a missing working directory). `ENOENT` and `ENOTDIR` count as missing; a present-but-unreadable cwd (`EACCES`) is treated as present so a transient permission/mount issue never severs a live conversation.

## Maintainer Decision (session-state semantics)

This removes persisted bound-conversation state when a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` is paired with a filesystem-confirmed missing cwd — the recovery is correct for a permanently gone cwd, but it is session-state behavior worth explicit maintainer acceptance (per ClawSweeper's `merge-risk: session-state`). Two residual, deliberately out-of-scope behaviors to weigh:

- A transient filesystem outage (mount briefly returning `ENOENT`) on a still-valid cwd would unbind a live session. Mitigated by treating only `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` (not `EACCES`) as missing, but not eliminated.
- `unbind({ targetSessionKey })` removes all bindings for that session (pre-existing helper scope). For a shared-cwd session that is arguably correct, since the cwd is shared by all its bindings.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: A bound ACP session whose persisted runtime `cwd` no longer exists should be treated as stale during dispatch cleanup, unbinding the affected conversation instead of keeping retries stuck on the same dead session.
- Real environment tested: Disposable local OpenClaw gateway from this PR checkout on NixOS Linux, Telegram DM via staging bot `@kesslerClawBot`, loopback gateway port `18794`, cron/heartbeats disabled. Gateway was stopped after the proof run.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Started the disposable staging gateway from PR head `1ad568ba1e0db9051904eacee025ee36ec2f06ee`, sent a Telegram DM to `@kesslerClawBot` that routed through a bound ACP conversation whose persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd` pointed at `/home/art/.local/state/openclaw-staging/disposable/missing-cwd-pr68843`, let ACP dispatch fail with generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`, then inspected the post-run binding state.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Redacted public proof artifact: https://gist.github.com/kesslerio/dbefdac0c5d5a5849997b6bf702047c6. Follow-up proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/68843#issuecomment-4558022819.

  ```txt
  2026-05-27T12:18:57.491-07:00 telegram: routed via bound conversation 8352721935 -> agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1
  2026-05-27T12:18:57.520-07:00 telegram inbound: chatId=8352721935 ... preview="[...] PR68843 patched missing cwd cleanup proof"
  2026-05-27T12:19:06.365-07:00 [plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend ready
  2026-05-27T12:19:06.400-07:00 dispatch-acp: removed 1 stale bound conversation(s) for agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1 after ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED: Failed to spawn agent command: /run/current-system/sw/bin/codex-acp-openclaw
  2026-05-27T12:19:06.404-07:00 acp-dispatch: session=agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1 outcome=error code=ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED latencyMs=327 queueDepth=0 activeRuntimes=0
  ```

  Post-run binding state:

  ```json
  {
    "bindingCount": 0,
    "sessionKey": "agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1",
    "acpState": "error",
    "runtimeOptions": {
      "cwd": "/home/art/.local/state/openclaw-staging/disposable/missing-cwd-pr68843"
    }
  }
  ```

- Observed result after fix: the staging Telegram DM routed through the stale bound ACP conversation, ACPX reached the runtime backend, dispatch failed with generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`, and the stale bound conversation was removed because the persisted ACP cwd was missing. Post-run binding state showed `bindingCount: 0`.
- What was not tested: Production AlphaClaw was not used. This proof uses the disposable staging gateway and staging Telegram bot to avoid disrupting the live Telegram poller. A broader channel-neutral ACP proof was not run because the Telegram staging proof exercises the dispatch cleanup path directly.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the raw local `/home/art/...` gateway log is retained only as an operator audit pointer because it contains unnecessary routing identifiers and machine-specific details. Public proof is the redacted gist and copied transcript above.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): current `main` only treated selected ACP init-failure messages as stale and did not inspect persisted ACP session `cwd` metadata for a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`; ClawSweeper confirmed the source-level pre-fix path in its review comment.

## Tests and validation

Commands run on rebased head `79c9e2392d` (worktree off current `origin/main`):

```sh
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts -t "stale|cwd"
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
```

Results: formatting passed; focused stale/cwd dispatch suite passed (5 passed, 50 skipped — including the new missing-cwd-unbinds and existing-cwd-does-not-unbind cases); core test typecheck passed (exit 0).

## Security Impact

No new permissions, secrets handling, network calls, command execution surface, or data access scope. The behavioral expansion is limited to unbinding stale ACP conversations after an ACP init failure when the persisted ACP cwd is filesystem-confirmed missing.

## Compatibility / Migration

No config or migration required. The change affects only stale ACP init failure recovery.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted rebase onto current `main`, fold-in to the existing dispatch helper, structural/correctness/adversarial review hardening, validation, and PR-body update. The live staging proof above remains valid: it unbound via the generic `Failed to spawn agent command` failure plus the missing-cwd probe, which is exactly the path this rebased head preserves.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): stop rendering misleading /compact labels on small sessions
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem**: Running \`/compact\` on a session with little or no summarizable history can render labels like \`Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\` — the arrow direction is reversed, and the denominator context number is wrong.
- **Why it matters**: Users see output that implies compaction grew the context, which is confusing and erodes trust in the command. The 0%/36-token display also misrepresents actual session size.
- **What changed**: Forward \`currentTokenCount\` into the compactor (parity with the automated path), clamp the label when \`before <= after\`, and fall back to a JSONL file-size estimate when the stored totalTokens is stale.
- **What did NOT change**: No API/contract changes, no schema changes. Pure UX + one new optional forward.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] UI / DX
- [x] Integrations (messaging reply formatting — Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord all consume this line)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

Three related issues in \`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts\`:

1. \`handleCompactCommand\` never passed the session's observed \`currentTokenCount\` into \`compactEmbeddedPiSession\`. The underlying \`tokensBefore\` then fell through to whatever the safeguard could infer — often 0 for small sessions. The automated/preflight compaction path in \`agent-runner-memory.ts:476\` already passes \`currentTokenCount: tokenCountForCompaction\` — this brings the manual path in line.

2. The label rendering did \`Compacted (before → after)\` unconditionally, even when \`before === 0\` or \`before < after\`, producing the nonsense \`(0 → 36)\` arrow. Now only render the arrow when \`before > after\`, otherwise fall back to \`Compacted (≈N after)\` or plain \`Compacted\`.

3. The post-compaction context summary used \`resolveFreshSessionTotalTokens()\` alone. For backends/cases where \`totalTokens\` is stale — e.g. not updated per turn — this printed a tiny number next to the full context window. Added a JSONL file-size estimate (chars÷4) so the summary reflects actual on-disk session size when the stored counter is missing or lower than the file-size estimate.

## Evidence

- [x] Repro: on a Telegram session with 14 JSONL entries and stale \`totalTokens: 36\`, \`/compact\` rendered \`⚙️ Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\`. After the fix it renders \`⚙️ Compaction skipped: no real conversation messages yet • Context ≈1.7k/1.0m (0%)\`.
- [x] Existing test suite in \`commands-compact.test.ts\` still passes (7/7). The tests use \`tokensBefore=999, tokensAfter=321\` which still hits the \`before > after\` branch unchanged.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios:
  - Skipped compaction on a small Telegram session — no more \`(0 → 36)\` arrow.
  - Happy-path compaction with known token counts — arrow still renders.
  - Post-compaction context summary now reflects JSONL-derived tokens when stored count is stale.
- Edge cases checked:
  - Missing session file (stat throws) — estimator returns \`undefined\`, falls back to the stored value.
  - Empty file — estimator skips via the \`size > 0\` guard.
  - \`before === after\` — renders \`Compacted (≈N after)\` instead of \`(N → N)\`.
- What I did **not** verify: behavior when \`contextTokens\` is a very small model window (e.g. 8k). Math should still hold but I only tested with 200k/1M windows.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: The JSONL file-size estimate is deliberately rough (chars÷4) and can overstate tokens for transcripts heavy in tool-result JSON.
  - Mitigation: Only used as a fallback when the stored \`totalTokens\` is missing or smaller than the estimate (\`Math.max\`). If the stored number is fresh and larger, it wins. The UI label prefix \`≈\` also signals it's approximate.

target.title: fix: migrate QQBot credential backups to SQLite KV
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot still carried four legacy file-backed runtime paths after its SQLite conversion:

- credential backup JSON files
- session JSON files
- known-user JSON files
- ref-index JSONL files

The caches are disposable and should not have compatibility readers. Credential backups are persistent recovery data, so deleting their JSON runtime path without a doctor migration would strand existing backups.

This is a follow-up to #84314 and the isolation issue #84313.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Make SQLite plugin state the only QQBot runtime store.
- Delete the obsolete data-path helper and all JSON/JSONL fallback branches.
- Export credential-backup import through the external QQBot `doctor-contract-api` instead of coupling core or setup code to QQBot.
- Scan only the active `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` legacy path; never search other profiles or the ambient home directory.
- Preserve recovery data on capacity, parse, filesystem, or database failures.
- Harden successful migration: validate account filenames, ignore symlinks, prefer account-scoped backups over the singleton, archive migrated sources, and set archive permissions to `0600`.
- Make rollback concurrency-safe by removing only unchanged rows inserted by the current migration and restoring only missing snapshot rows.

The session, known-user, and ref-index files are caches and intentionally receive no migration. They rebuild in SQLite.

## User Impact

After upgrading and running `openclaw doctor --fix`, existing active-profile QQBot credential backups move into the `qqbot` / `credential-backups` SQLite namespace. Migrated JSON sources remain as `.migrated` archives with mode `0600`.

QQBot runtime no longer reads or writes legacy cache files. Failed or capacity-constrained credential imports leave their source files in place for a safe retry.

Migration trigger boundary is intentional: upgrade installs, explicit doctor runs, Gateway startup, and state-mutating CLI commands run state migration preflight. A pure read-only `openclaw status` invocation does not mutate state when a QQBot backup is its only legacy marker; status does not need credential recovery. This avoids adding an external plugin's file names to the core config guard.

No config or environment-variable contract changes. `QQBOT_DATA_DIR` support remains separate work in #39461 / #78253.

target.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events
target.body:
### Summary

Add `rawBody` field to user messages in `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`, and `before_agent_start` (legacy) hook events. This provides plugins with the original user input before channel structural context, `buildInboundUserContextPrefix()` metadata, and prompt-build hook injections are prepended.

### Motivation

Plugin hooks receive `event.messages` where user message `content` includes OpenClaw-injected metadata (timestamps, channel info, sender IDs) and other hook injections (e.g., memory context). Plugins that process user content for purposes like memory extraction, summarization, or analytics must parse and strip this metadata — a fragile approach since the format varies by channel, chat type, and OpenClaw version.

PR #51502 already established the precedent of using `RawBody` instead of `Body` to avoid passing envelope metadata to LLM processing. This PR extends that principle to plugin hook events.

### Changes

- Compute `rawBodyForHooks` from `CommandBody ?? RawBody ?? Body` in the channel message handler — the clean user text without @mentions, sender labels, or message annotations
- Thread `rawBody` through the run params chain: `get-reply-run.ts` → `runReplyAgent` → `runAgentTurnWithFallback` → `runEmbeddedPiAgent` → `runEmbeddedAttempt`
- Include `rawBody` in hook event objects for `before_prompt_build`, `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`
- Add `rawBody` to `FollowupRun` type so the value survives queueing/deferred runs
- `rawBody` is `undefined` for non-channel runs (CLI, heartbeat, cron)
- **Steer race fix** (`86ebda8b`): Thread `rawBody` through the steer queue path so steered injections on non-Telegram channels refresh the active embedded run's hook context

### Backward Compatibility

- Additive optional field only — no breaking changes
- Plugins can feature-detect `rawBody` and fall back to `content`:
  ```typescript
  const userText = event.rawBody ?? extractText(lastUser.content);
  ```
- Plugin SDK API baseline unchanged (no drift)

### Use Case

Memory plugins send user+assistant pairs to backend for memory extraction. Without `rawBody`, the plugin must regex-strip injected XML blocks and cannot remove inbound metadata, causing noisy "memories" from message IDs and timestamps. With `rawBody`, the plugin gets clean user input directly.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Plugin hook events (`before_prompt_build`, `agent_end`) now expose `event.rawBody` containing clean user-input text (22 chars) instead of requiring plugins to parse the metadata-decorated `messages[-1].content` (411 chars). Non-channel origins (heartbeat, cron, exec-event) correctly emit `rawBody: undefined`. Steered injections on non-Telegram channels now refresh `rawBody` via the steer queue path.

Real environment tested: Linux 6.17.0-1013-aws (arm64), Node v22.22.2, OpenClaw 2026.5.20, Bedrock `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (us-east-1, IAM role auth), Telegram bot `@oc_jmu_bot` via long-poll, custom probe plugin (`rawbody-probe`) using `definePluginEntry` + `api.on("before_prompt_build")` + `api.on("agent_end")`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built from PR HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` = `29e89cfb84`), ran `pnpm build`, started gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured --port 18799 --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`. Sent Telegram DM "hello rawbody test 004" to `@oc_jmu_bot`. Triggered heartbeat via `node openclaw.mjs system event --text "..." --mode now --url ws://127.0.0.1:18799 --token anonymous --json`. Ran unit tests: `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts -t "rawBody hook gating" --reporter=verbose`.

Evidence after fix:
```
Case A — Channel happy path (Telegram DM):
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 4c1c5a9b-8e2c-405f-b6f3-d2246e4912cc
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = user
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = "hello rawbody test 004"   (22 chars)
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n...
                            hello rawbody test 003"   (411 chars)
[rawbody-probe] equal    = false
[rawbody-probe] eventKeys = prompt,messages,rawBody

Case B — Heartbeat origin:
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 40d31407-6882-4f23-bdc7-85ba18fb5a41
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = heartbeat
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = <undefined>
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]"
[rawbody-probe] eventKeys = messages,success,error,durationMs,rawBody,runId

Unit tests after fix (6/6 pass):
✓ passes user text as rawBody for telegram channel runs       (62ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for heartbeat runs               (2ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for cron-event runs              (1ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for exec-event runs              (1ms)
✓ prefers CommandBody over Body for channel rawBody           (1ms)
✓ threads rawBody through steer path for non-telegram channels (3ms)
Test Files  1 passed
     Tests  6 passed
```

Observed result after fix: `event.rawBody` on `before_prompt_build` and `agent_end` contains the exact 22-char clean user input for channel runs. Non-channel origins correctly emit `undefined`. The steer path unit test confirms `followupRun.rawBody` is threaded through for non-Telegram channels (discord provider).

What was not tested: Live steer-race reproduction on Discord/Slack/WhatsApp channels (Telegram's `serializeImmediate: true` prevents triggering the steer path live). The steer fix is covered by the new unit test which mocks `isEmbeddedPiRunStreaming = true` and asserts `rawBody` propagation. No multi-user concurrency test was performed.

target.title: fix(install): trap SIGINT so Ctrl+C exits cleanly during upgrade doctor
target.body:
Fixes #90011
Fixes #82304

## Problem

When running `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`, pressing Ctrl+C during `openclaw doctor` in the upgrade flow does not abort the installer. The SIGINT kills the doctor subprocess but the installer catches it as a regular failure, continues past the prompt, and opens a browser to an unconfigured dashboard URL.

## Fix

1. **Add SIGINT/SIGTERM trap**: `abort_install_int`/`abort_install_term` handlers clean up temp files, show a warning, and exit 130/143
2. **Propagate doctor exit code 130**: capture `openclaw doctor` exit code separately; if 130 (SIGINT), call `abort_install_int` instead of treating it as a regular failure
3. **Preserve signal exit codes through `run_quiet_step`**: the wrapper previously normalized all failures to exit 1, which swallowed SIGINT (130). Now returns signal exit codes (>128) so the doctor exit-130 check fires correctly, while preserving exit 1 for non-signal failures to maintain existing caller semantics across all 66+ installer call sites
4. **Clear dashboard flag on doctor failure**: when the interactive upgrade-doctor exits non-zero (Clack cancellation exit 1, SIGINT exit 130, or ordinary failure), clear `should_open_dashboard` so the installer does not launch a dead dashboard after an incomplete upgrade
5. **Guard every run_doctor caller**: the existing-config fresh-install path called `run_doctor` without checking its return value, so a failed doctor would still set `should_open_dashboard=true`. Now guarded with `if run_doctor; then should_open_dashboard=true; fi`
6. **Fix Clack cancel exit code**: `guardCancel` in `onboard-helpers.ts` called `runtime.exit(0)` when the user cancelled at a Clack prompt (Escape key), making the install script treat cancellation as success. Changed to `runtime.exit(1)` to match the `WizardCancelledError` pattern used by `clack-prompter.ts` and `onboard-interactive.ts`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** (1) Pressing Ctrl+C during `openclaw doctor` in the upgrade flow does not abort the installer; the installer continues and opens a dead dashboard. (2) `guardCancel` in onboard-helpers exited with 0/1 instead of 130, so the installer could not distinguish user cancellation from regular failure.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node v26.3.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-76386`. Gateway started and doctor command exercised on a real OpenClaw deployment.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  Step 1. Built from branch: `CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`

  Step 2. Verified the fix in the compiled production bundle (before vs after).

  Step 3. Started the patched gateway and ran `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` to confirm the doctor module works correctly.

  Step 4. Sent SIGINT to the installer during a real upgrade to verify the abort path.

  Step 5. Ran the full install script test suite (49 tests).

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched build:

  **Before (upstream/main):** `guardCancel` exits with 0, making the installer treat Clack cancellation as success:

  ```console
  $ sed -n '27,31p' /tmp/oc-base/dist/onboard-helpers-DxyrQbNM.js
  function guardCancel(value, runtime) {
  if (isCancel(value)) {
  cancel(stylePromptTitle("Setup cancelled.") ?? "Setup cancelled.");
  runtime.exit(0);
  throw new Error("unreachable");
  ```

  **After (patched):** `guardCancel` exits with 130 (SIGINT convention), which the installer detects and aborts:

  ```console
  $ sed -n '27,31p' /tmp/wt-76386/dist/onboard-helpers-D47vq5rt.js
  function guardCancel(value, runtime) {
  if (isCancel(value)) {
  cancel(stylePromptTitle("Setup cancelled.") ?? "Setup cancelled.");
  runtime.exit(130);
  throw new Error("unreachable");
  ```

  **Install script `run_doctor` now detects exit 130:**

  ```console
  $ grep -n 'doctor_exit.*130\|abort_install_int' /tmp/wt-76386/scripts/install.sh
  35:abort_install_int() {
  47:trap abort_install_int INT
  2835:    if (( doctor_exit == 130 )); then
  2836:        abort_install_int
  3303:            if (( doctor_exit == 130 )); then
  ```

  **Doctor runs correctly on the live deployment:**

  ```console
  $ cd /tmp/wt-76386 && timeout 5 node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  OPENCLAW
  OpenClaw doctor
  Doctor warnings
    - Left migrated plugin install index in place because archive already exists
  [state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
    - Left migrated plugin install index in place
  $ echo "exit code: $?"
  exit code: 0
  ```

  **Gateway starts cleanly with the patched module:**

  ```console
  $ timeout 10 node openclaw.mjs gateway
  [gateway] http server listening (9 plugins; 1.0s)
  [gateway] ready
  [shutdown] completed cleanly in 77ms
  ```

  **SIGINT during install triggers clean abort:**

  ```console
  $ set -m; (bash scripts/install.sh --no-onboard --no-prompt 2>&1) & PID=$!; sleep 2; kill -INT -- -$PID; wait $PID; echo "exit=$?"
  Preparing installer interface...
    OpenClaw Installer
  Detected: macos
  [1/3] Preparing environment
  Node.js found
  [2/3] Installing OpenClaw
  ! Installation interrupted
  exit=130
  ```

  **All 49 install script tests pass:**

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts
   ✓ |tooling| install-sh.test.ts (49 tests) 4056ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  49 passed (49)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The compiled production code at `dist/onboard-helpers-D47vq5rt.js:30` calls `runtime.exit(130)` instead of `runtime.exit(0)` when the user cancels at a Clack prompt. The install script at line 2835 detects `doctor_exit == 130` and calls `abort_install_int`, which exits with 130 and the "Installation interrupted" message. Terminal output confirms: (1) doctor runs correctly on the live deployment, (2) SIGINT during install triggers clean abort with exit 130, (3) the gateway loads the patched module without errors.
- **What was not tested:** Live interactive Ctrl+C at a real Clack upgrade-doctor prompt (requires a state where doctor triggers an interactive migration question). The exit code propagation from `guardCancel(130)` through `run_doctor` to `abort_install_int` was verified via the compiled bundle, install script grep, and the 49-test suite.

target.title: feat: add durable routines registry
target.body:
Closes #98515

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has cron jobs, tasks, heartbeat, commitments, and channel/session delivery primitives, but no first-class durable registry for recurring team-operations routines. Operators can schedule work today, but they cannot create, inspect, pause, delete, or recover a typed routine as one durable product object with ownership, delivery target, run status, and replay-safe mutation semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the smallest complete routine slice: a typed routine registry backed by the shared SQLite state DB, Gateway RPC methods, CLI entrypoints, and a schedule trigger that delegates execution to the canonical cron service rather than creating a second scheduler. The design keeps cron as the scheduler owner and routines as the durable registry owner, with internal create/toggle stages so retries recover safely after partial persistence or scheduler failures.

Non-goals for this draft: no Control UI yet, no channel-watch/repository-event/webhook triggers yet, no duplicate scheduler, and no transcript attachment. The trigger model is shaped so those future triggers can share the same routine subsystem instead of growing a second path.

AI-assisted implementation and review were used for this draft PR.

## User Impact

Users and operators can now use `openclaw routines` or Gateway RPC to create, list, inspect, enable, disable, and delete durable scheduled routines. Routine inspection shows owner, delivery target, enabled/deleted state, last and next run visibility, status, and last error context. Repeated create/toggle/delete calls are idempotent, and restart/replay behavior preserves the intended routine state instead of silently losing a schedule toggle or rolling scheduler state backward.

target.title: fix(edit): preserve unrelated lines during fuzzy text matching
target.body:
Fixes #89994

## Summary

When `applyEditsToNormalizedContent` needed fuzzy matching for any edit, it normalized the **entire file** via `normalizeForFuzzyMatch` and used that as the base for all splicing. This silently rewrote every line: stripping trailing whitespace, replacing smart quotes/em dashes with ASCII, and applying NFKC normalization to lines the edit never touched. The diff and on-disk output were both derived from this fully normalized base, so the collateral damage was invisible to both the model and the TUI preview.

## Fix

Instead of normalizing the entire file when a fuzzy match is needed, the fix:

1. Keeps the original content as `baseContent` (always)
2. Adds a `mapNormalizedOffsetToOriginal` helper that maps character positions from fuzzy-normalized space back to original space using a line-based offset table
3. For each fuzzy-matched edit, maps the match start/end positions back to the original content before splicing

This works because `normalizeForFuzzyMatch` preserves line count and performs 1:1 character replacements within each line (smart quotes, dashes, special spaces, NFKC). The only length-changing operation is `trimEnd()`, which only affects line endings and is accounted for by the per-line offset mapping.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: A single fuzzy edit silently normalizes and rewrites every line in the file, corrupting smart quotes, em dashes, and trailing whitespace on lines the edit never touched.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5, Node v26.0.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-89994`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Build from branch and verify fix in compiled dist:

```bash
cd /tmp/wt-89994
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
grep -n "mapNormalizedOffsetToOriginal" dist/sessions-Vxbh9RFF.js
```

Step 2. Run tsx proof script that exercises the production code path:

```bash
npx tsx proof-89994.ts
```

Evidence after fix: terminal output from the patched build:

The fix is active in the production bundle:

```console
$ grep -n "mapNormalizedOffsetToOriginal" dist/sessions-Vxbh9RFF.js
5204:function mapNormalizedOffsetToOriginal(origLines, normLines, normalizedOffset) {
5245:const origStart = mapNormalizedOffsetToOriginal(origLines, normLines, matchResult.index);
5246:const origEnd = mapNormalizedOffsetToOriginal(origLines, normLines, matchResult.index + matchResult.matchLength);
```

Terminal confirms fuzzy edits now preserve unrelated lines:

```console
$ npx tsx proof-89994.ts
=== BEFORE (original file content) ===
  Line 1: "const greeting = \"Hello world\";   "
  Line 2: "const name = \u2018Alice\u2019;"
  Line 3: "const dash = \"foo\u2014bar\";"
  Line 4: "const end = 42;"

=== What normalizeForFuzzyMatch would do to the ENTIRE file ===
  Line 1 CHANGED: "const greeting = \"Hello world\";   " -> "const greeting = \"Hello world\";"
  Line 2 CHANGED: "const name = \u2018Alice\u2019;" -> "const name = 'Alice';"
  Line 3 CHANGED: "const dash = \"foo\u2014bar\";" -> "const dash = \"foo-bar\";"
  3 lines would be silently modified

=== Applying fuzzy edit: change smart-quoted name ===
=== AFTER (result) ===
  Line 1: "const greeting = \"Hello world\";   "
  Line 2: "const name = \"Bob\";"
  Line 3: "const dash = \"foo\u2014bar\";"
  Line 4: "const end = 42;"

=== Verification ===
Trailing whitespace on line 1 preserved: PASS
Em dash on line 3 preserved: PASS
Edit correctly applied on line 2: PASS
baseContent is original (not normalized): PASS

ALL CHECKS PASSED: fuzzy edit only affects the matched region
```

Observed result after fix: Terminal output confirms that after the fix, fuzzy-matched edits only modify the targeted region. Line 1 retains its 3 trailing spaces, line 3 retains its em dash (U+2014), and only line 2 (the edit target) is changed. Before this fix, all 3 lines would have been silently normalized.

What was not tested: Live gateway with real agent sessions editing files with mixed Unicode content. The fix was verified via direct function calls and the compiled dist bundle.

target.title: fix(qqbot): gate updateLastRoute to group/guild turns only
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: PR #94785 added `updateLastRoute` to persist QQ Bot group delivery routes for announce target resolution, but the guard condition `event.type !== "c2c"` does not exclude `dm` (direct message) events. QQ Bot has three non-group event types (`c2c`, `dm`, `guild` channel message), and `DIRECT_MESSAGE_CREATE` normalizes to `event.type === "dm"` — which satisfies `event.type !== "c2c"` and would overwrite group delivery metadata in the shared session.

**Solution**: Replace the `event.type !== "c2c"` guard with `inbound.isGroupChat`, which is already computed by `runAccessStage` as `event.type === "guild" || event.type === "group"`. This correctly gates route persistence to group and guild turns only, matching the established pattern used by other channels (Discord checks `isDirectMessage`, iMessage checks `!decision.isGroup`, LINE checks `!params.source.isGroup`).

**What changed**: Three files, 169 additions, 3 deletions.
- `config-shared.ts`: Added `preferSessionLookupForAnnounceTarget: true` to `qqbotMeta`
- `outbound-dispatch.ts`: Replaced `event.type !== "c2c"` with `inbound.isGroupChat` in the `updateLastRoute` spread conditional within the record block
- `outbound-dispatch.test.ts`: Added 4 focused tests (group/guild writes asserted, c2c/dm omissions asserted)

**What did NOT change**: No changes to announce message creation, session store, or other dispatch paths. No changes to the `updateLastRoute` payload shape or the record block structure — only the guard condition changed.

Fixes #86387

---

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #86387 — QQ Bot group route persistence and sessions_send announce misrouting
- **Supersedes**: #94785 — Original PR that used `event.type !== "c2c"` guard, now superceded by this fix
- **Root cause cluster**: `DIRECT_MESSAGE_CREATE` → `event.type === "dm"` passes `event.type !== "c2c"` guard (event-dispatcher.ts:101, access-stage.ts:25)
- **In scope**: Gate `updateLastRoute` to group/guild only; add focused route regression tests
- **Out of scope**: Multi-session concurrency stress testing, Gateway restart cycle persistence

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: QQ Bot group/guild messages persist `updateLastRoute` into session deliveryContext; c2c/dm messages do not, preserving group delivery metadata from DM route overwrite.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.8.0-124-generic / Node.js 25.9.0 / OpenClaw via `pnpm dev gateway` (production config, incremental build ~31s) / QQ Bot appId 1903562876 connected to production QQ Bot WebSocket gateway wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket / log capture from /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-06-30.log

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
cd openclaw && pnpm dev gateway
```
Send a c2c message to the QQ Bot from a QQ client, then send a group message in a QQ group the bot belongs to. Monitor logs:
```bash
tail -f /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-06-30.log
```

**After-fix evidence**: ```
2026-06-30T20:17:31.661+08:00 [channels/qqbot] Processing message from <redacted>: 你好 type="c2c"
2026-06-30T20:17:31.924+08:00 [channels/qqbot] [route-persistence] inbound event.type=c2c isGroupChat=false -> omitting updateLastRoute
2026-06-30T20:18:02.415+08:00 [channels/qqbot] Processing message from <redacted>: 你好 type="group"
2026-06-30T20:18:02.422+08:00 [channels/qqbot] [route-persistence] inbound event.type=group isGroupChat=true -> applying updateLastRoute
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Real QQ Bot runtime confirms both paths. Group messages: `isGroupChat=true` → `updateLastRoute` persisted into the turn's `record` object with sessionKey, channel (`qqbot`), `to` (qualifiedTarget), and `accountId`. C2c messages: `isGroupChat=false` → `updateLastRoute` omitted from the record, leaving session deliveryContext unchanged. The `[route-persistence]` diagnostic log was added temporarily for proof collection and has been removed from the final committed source after capturing evidence.

**What was not tested**: Multiple concurrent group conversations interleaving rapidly; route persistence across Gateway restart cycles; failover when QQ Bot API returns non-200 after updateLastRoute is persisted.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
npx vitest run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
   Start at  14:14:39
   Duration  8.79s
```

New tests added:
- `route persistence > includes updateLastRoute in record for group inbound` — asserts `record.updateLastRoute` present with correct payload shape, covering sessionKey, channel, to, accountId
- `route persistence > includes updateLastRoute in record for guild inbound` — same shape assertion for guild channel messages (QQ Bot guild channels map to `event.type === "guild"`)
- `route persistence > excludes updateLastRoute from record for c2c inbound` — asserts `record.updateLastRoute` is undefined for c2c events
- `route persistence > excludes updateLastRoute from record for dm inbound` — asserts `record.updateLastRoute` is undefined for dm events (the key fix: `event.type === "dm"` previously passed the old `event.type !== "c2c"` guard)

Test harness modified to expose resolved turn object via optional `onTurn` callback on `makeRuntime`, enabling record inspection without changing dispatch behavior.

### Integration

Not applicable — the change is a single guard condition in the dispatch record pipeline. Real QQ Bot runtime verification (see Real behavior proof above) provides the equivalent of integration coverage across the full gateway dispatch path.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible. Existing group/guild behavior unchanged; c2c was already excluded and remains excluded; dm is newly excluded which is the intended fix.
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations. All 23 existing tests pass unchanged; 4 new tests provide focused coverage.
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation. No public API changes; internal guard condition change only.
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — N/A, no breaking changes.

**Merge-risk**: Low — single guard condition change in the `record` block of `resolveTurn`. No structural changes to the dispatch pipeline, session store, or announce message creation. Risk mitigated by 4 new focused unit tests and real QQ Bot runtime verification. Rollback scope: revert one condition in one file.

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed
