target.title: Fix Telegram plugin callback routing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Telegram inline-button callbacks such as `code-agent:<uuid>` can fall through to the generic callback text path when the global plugin interactive handler state is empty, causing raw `callback_data: code-agent:<uuid>` messages to be sent instead of routing to the OpenClaw Code Agent plugin handler.

## Why This Change Was Made
The fix restores plugin interactive handlers from the live plugin registry before reporting an interactive callback as unmatched, keeps the existing raw callback_data fallback for callbacks no plugin claims, and makes registry-stored interactive handlers participate in loader snapshot/restore rollback so failed plugin registration cannot leave executable handlers reachable.

## User Impact
Telegram users pressing OpenClaw Code Agent inline buttons should get the intended plugin action, including button cleanup, instead of seeing raw callback data text in the chat. Failed plugin registration also no longer leaves stale interactive handlers available through the registry-backed recovery path.

## Evidence
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/loader.test.ts -- -t "rolls back global side effects when registration fails"`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/interactive.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts -- -t "restores active registry interactive handlers before reporting unmatched callbacks|routes code-agent callbacks to plugin handlers and clears original buttons"`

## Notes
This is the clean re-cut of the single task commit onto current origin/main, avoiding the release/2026.6.10 branch history that made the previous worktree appear thousands of commits ahead.

target.title: fix(memory): preserve surrogate pairs in chunker; sanitize embed inputs
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix the outer coarse-split loop in `chunkMarkdown` so it does not bisect a UTF-16 surrogate pair (root cause of indexing stalls).
- Add a defensive `stripUnpairedSurrogates` sanitizer at the embed boundary (the safety net #27753 originally requested).
- Tests for both, including a new regression test that triggers the exact code path the existing surrogate-pair test missed.

Closes #27753.
Fixes #65782.

## Why

Memory indexing stalls permanently for any agent whose content contains an emoji or supplementary-plane character that the chunker happens to split across a surrogate-pair boundary. `openclaw memory status` reports the index as `clean / no issues` while ~98% of sessions are unindexed.

End-to-end symptom (verbose):

```
[memory] embeddings: batch start  (×N)
Memory index failed (<agent>): openai embeddings failed: 500
{"error":{"message":"... 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\\ud83c'
in position 3229: surrogates not allowed ..."}}
```

Two failure modes compound:

1. **Chunker** (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`) — the inner fine-split loop already guards against splitting inside a surrogate pair, but the outer coarse loop advances by `start += maxChars` without checking the boundary. When the cut lands inside e.g. an emoji like 🌸 (`U+1F338` = `\uD83C\uDF38`), the chunk ends with a lone high surrogate and the next begins with a lone low surrogate. The existing surrogate-pair test (`"does not break surrogate pairs when splitting long CJK lines"`) does not catch this because it uses an all-surrogate-pair line — the high `estimateStringChars` weight forces the inner pass, which is correct.
2. **Embedding HTTP path** — Python JSON encoders (e.g. via LiteLLM proxies) reject lone surrogates with a 500 wrapping a `UnicodeEncodeError`. The retry policy only matches `rate_limit | 429 | 5\d\d | cloudflare | tokens per day`, but the body shape is a connect-error, not a transient one — and the indexer is transactional, so a single bad batch rolls back the entire run. Every subsequent `openclaw memory index` invocation reproduces the same failure.

## What changed

### `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`

```diff
- for (let start = 0; start < line.length; start += maxChars) {
-   const coarse = line.slice(start, start + maxChars);
+ for (let start = 0; start < line.length; ) {
+   let coarseEnd = Math.min(line.length, start + maxChars);
+   // Avoid splitting inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK Extension B+).
+   if (coarseEnd < line.length) {
+     const lastCode = line.charCodeAt(coarseEnd - 1);
+     if (lastCode >= 0xd800 && lastCode <= 0xdbff) {
+       coarseEnd += 1; // include the trailing low surrogate
+     }
+   }
+   const coarse = line.slice(start, coarseEnd);
+   start = coarseEnd;
```

Mirrors the existing inner-loop guard at the same file/line. New regression test (`"does not break surrogate pairs at the coarse split boundary (issue #27753)"`) constructs a line of `39 ASCII + 🌸 + 39 ASCII` so the outer cut at `start + maxChars = 40` lands between the high and low surrogate. Without the fix, the test fails by producing chunks containing lone surrogates.

### `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts`

Adds a tiny exported helper:

```ts
export function stripUnpairedSurrogates(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(
    /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/g,
    "\uFFFD",
  );
}
```

…and applies it at the entry of `embedBatchWithRetry` and `embedBatchInputsWithRetry`. This is the change #27753 originally requested. It protects against any other code path that might produce a lone surrogate (LLM tool output, file ingestion, future chunkers) — chunker-only fix is necessary but not sufficient.

Adds `manager-embedding-ops.test.ts` with focused unit tests for the helper (preserves valid pairs, replaces lone high/low surrogates, handles reversed pairs, no-op on empty/non-string).

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live on installed runtime (`openclaw 2026.4.5`) by patching the equivalent bundled artifact under `dist/manager-CKYnEo0k.js` and running `openclaw memory index --agent <id>`:

  | | before | after |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | clawdea files | 6 | **166** |
  | clawdea chunks | 93 | **4584** |
  | dev files | 2 | **17** |
  | dev chunks | 251 | **588** |

  `openclaw memory search` works end-to-end after the fix.
- [ ] CI runs `pnpm test` against the new unit tests in `extensions/memory-core` and `packages/memory-host-sdk`.
- [ ] Existing surrogate-pair test (`"does not break surrogate pairs when splitting long CJK lines"`) still passes.

## Notes for reviewers

- I did not run `pnpm install` locally to execute vitest — the runtime fix is verified live, and the new tests follow the same vitest patterns as adjacent files (`manager-embedding-cache.test.ts`, `internal.test.ts`).
- The retry-policy gap (`fetch failed` / `UnicodeEncodeError` 500 not retried) is a separate concern tracked in #56815 / #58255 — out of scope for this PR. With the chunker + sanitizer in place, the original failure no longer reaches the retry path.

target.title: fix: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC...
target.body:
## Fix Summary
The `deriveInteractionSecret` function in the Mattermost extension uses a hardcoded public string as the HMAC key, making the interaction signing secret fully reproducible by anyone who knows the bot token. An attacker who obtains the bot token can forge valid `_token` values, craft arbitrary button-click POST requests to the gateway's interaction endpoint, and trigger agent system events (`core.system.enqueueSystemEvent`) as if a legitimate user clicked an approved Mattermost button.

## Issue Linkage
Fixes #64545

## Security Snapshot
- CVSS v3.1: 7.1 (High)
- CVSS v4.0: 7.1 (High)

## Implementation Details
### Files Changed
- `extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema-core.ts` (+1/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema.test.ts` (+19/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/accounts.test.ts` (+23/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/accounts.ts` (+8/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.test.ts` (+20/-17)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts` (+23/-10)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts` (+2/-3)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts` (+8/-2)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/types.ts` (+2/-0)

### Technical Analysis
1. Obtain the Mattermost bot token (available via the Mattermost admin panel, gateway environment variables, or any configuration leak).
2. Reproduce the derivation: `derivedSecret = HMAC-SHA256("openclaw-mattermost-interactions", botToken)` — this is deterministic and requires no further gateway access.
3. Construct an action context matching an existing interactive post, e.g., `{"action_id": "approve", "post_id": "<target_post_id>", "channel_id": "<target_channel_id>"}`.
4. Compute the forged token: `_token = HMAC-SHA256(derivedSecret, JSON.stringify(sortedContext))`.
5. POST a crafted payload to `http://<gateway-host>:<gatewayPort>/mattermost/interactions/<accountId>` with the forged `_token` field.
6. `verifyInteractionToken` at `interactions.ts:165-175` passes; the handler dispatches `core.system.enqueueSystemEvent` to the agent as if a legitimate user clicked an approved button.

## Validation Evidence
- Command: `pnpm exec oxlint src/ && pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test`
- Status: passed (with pre-existing baseline failures)

## Risk and Compatibility
- non-breaking; no known regression impact

## AI-Assisted Disclosure
- AI-assisted: yes
- Model: github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Mattermost interaction tokens should no longer be forgeable from knowledge of the bot token; the branch now uses a generated or configured interaction secret instead of the old deterministic `HMAC-SHA256("openclaw-mattermost-interactions", botToken)` derivation.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on the rebased PR head `e261bcfab6de7ff05d18d2493ea60aedf234498d`, running the real Mattermost interaction module through Node with `tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'import { createHmac } from "node:crypto"; import { ensureInteractionSecret, generateInteractionToken, verifyInteractionToken } from "./extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts"; const botToken = "redacted-bot-token-for-proof"; const oldDerivedSecret = createHmac("sha256", "openclaw-mattermost-interactions").update(botToken).digest("hex"); const generatedSecret = ensureInteractionSecret("proof-account"); const configuredSecret = ensureInteractionSecret("configured-account", "configured-proof-secret"); const context = { action_id: "approve", proof: "after-fix" }; const validToken = generateInteractionToken(context, "proof-account"); const oldForgedToken = createHmac("sha256", oldDerivedSecret).update(JSON.stringify(context)).digest("hex"); console.log(JSON.stringify({ generatedSecretLength: generatedSecret.length, generatedSecretIsHex: /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(generatedSecret), generatedSecretMatchesOldBotTokenDerivation: generatedSecret === oldDerivedSecret, configuredSecretPreserved: configuredSecret === "configured-proof-secret", generatedTokenVerifies: verifyInteractionToken(context, validToken, "proof-account"), oldBotTokenDerivedForgeryVerifies: verifyInteractionToken(context, oldForgedToken, "proof-account") }, null, 2));'
```

- Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "generatedSecretLength": 64,
  "generatedSecretIsHex": true,
  "generatedSecretMatchesOldBotTokenDerivation": false,
  "configuredSecretPreserved": true,
  "generatedTokenVerifies": true,
  "oldBotTokenDerivedForgeryVerifies": false
}
```

- Observed result after fix: The generated interaction secret is random-looking 64-character hex and does not equal the old bot-token-derived secret. A token generated with the new per-account secret verifies, while a token forged from the old bot-token-derived secret does not verify.
- What was not tested: Full live Mattermost server button-click delivery was not exercised in this local proof; focused local runtime proof and Mattermost extension tests were run for the changed interaction-secret behavior.

target.title: feat(mattermost): auto-engage on replies to the bot's own thread
target.body:
Related: #43456

## What Problem This Solves

In Mattermost channels and private/group threads, OpenClaw requires an explicit `@`-mention before it will respond (`requireMention` defaults to on). So when the bot posts a message and a user replies to it in the thread, the bot stays silent unless the user remembers to `@`-mention it again — an awkward, un-chatlike experience. Slack and Telegram users don't hit this, because those plugins already treat "replying to the bot" as addressing it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds reply-to-bot auto-engage to the Mattermost plugin: a thread reply now bypasses the mention requirement when the **thread-root post was authored by the bot**. Mattermost threads are flat — the current post model has no `parent_id` (only `root_id`), so unlike Slack (which uses the immediate parent) the only meaningful "who am I replying to" signal is the thread root's author. The websocket `posted` event omits that author, so it's fetched once via the Mattermost API — but only when a non-mentioned thread reply would otherwise be dropped, and the result is cached (reusing the plugin's existing channel/user lookup cache) so an active thread never re-fetches the same root.

The signal is folded into the plugin's existing bespoke mention gate. Non-goal: replying inside a human-rooted thread the bot merely participated in — that is intentionally left to the separate in-flight participated-thread change (#95552), which this composes with. Ships on by default; no new config or env.

## User Impact

In a Mattermost channel or group thread, users can now reply to one of the bot's own messages and get a response **without** re-`@`-mentioning it — matching how the Slack and Telegram plugins already behave. DMs, channels that don't require a mention, and explicit mentions are unaffected.

## Evidence

Local verification (run against the branch base; CI validates against current `main`):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost` → **29 files, 385 tests pass**. New coverage: the `replyToBot` gate input (engages over `requireMention`, and over the `onchar` trigger gate), the root-author detection helper (root authored by bot / by someone else / unfetchable / no thread root), and the new cached post lookup.
- `pnpm build` → clean (no type errors, no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on all changed files → clean.
- Docs updated (`docs/channels/mattermost.md`, `docs/channels/groups.md`) to document the new implicit reply-to-bot behavior; `format-docs --check` clean.

Not yet run at PR-open time: a real-Mattermost roundtrip (post as the bot in a thread, reply from another user without a mention, confirm the bot engages). See PR comments for roundtrip status.

The branch is based on an older `main` but touches no files changed upstream since, so it rebases cleanly.

target.title: feat: add monthly daily and stable release policy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot safely operate the new monthly daily/stable release model because release class, selector intent, protected policy authority, stable-line state, and publication evidence are not yet bound into one fail-closed contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the `YYYY.M.PATCH` release classifier, strict selector policy, immutable policy/publish/postpublish evidence, authenticated exact-ref verification, stable-line lifecycle tooling, and class-aware closeout across the public release workflows. The release-candidate helper also emits the complete authenticated public macOS validation handoff and the runbook documents exact recovery steps. The authoritative `release/stable-lines.json` genesis is intentionally deferred to the July bootstrap PR, so strict stable publication remains blocked until that metadata exists and a fresh candidate preflight is run.

## User Impact

Maintainers can run daily releases with `latest` while preparing and patching a trailing-month stable line from `stable/YYYY.M.33`. Daily releases cannot accidentally advance the stable selector, and stable publication fails closed unless the exact protected policy, source branch, tag, workflow runs, and immutable artifacts agree.

## Evidence

- [x] Automated: focused stable-release unit and workflow-contract suite passes after rebasing onto current `origin/main`.
- [x] Automated: workflow static checks, changed-file lint/format checks, YAML parsing, type checking, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [x] Automated: inherited mainline CI repairs pass focused tooling, channel, model-fallback, fast-mode, outcome-contract, and plugin-SDK streaming suites plus core and extension source/test type checks, lint, and formatting; Linux-only resolver isolation is delegated to CI because macOS ships Bash 3.2.
- [x] Downstream fork rehearsal: a `2026.6.33` stable line derived from this policy foundation completed an authenticated dry run and a publishing run from `stable/2026.6.33`, produced checksummed evidence assets, and installed the generated tarball in an isolated prefix.
  - [Non-publishing build/install run](https://github.com/kevinslin/openclaw/actions/runs/28420476933)
  - [Publishing run](https://github.com/kevinslin/openclaw/actions/runs/28421076528)
  - [Published fork release](https://github.com/kevinslin/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.6.33)
  - [Release manifest](https://github.com/kevinslin/openclaw/releases/download/v2026.6.33/fork-release-manifest.json) and [operation-verifier evidence](https://github.com/kevinslin/openclaw/releases/download/v2026.6.33/release-operation-verifier-v1.json)
  - Verified tag/source target: `5edaa7d6bbedd861dfd50f2da6afc88a13d73609`; downloaded SHA-256 checks passed; isolated install reported `OpenClaw 2026.6.33 (5edaa7d)`.
  - The manifest records `npmPublished: false` and `fullReleaseValidationRun: null`, matching the rehearsal's intentionally limited publication scope.
- [ ] Manual: exercise the official July bootstrap stable preflight after authoritative stable-line metadata lands (deferred bootstrap release gate).
- [ ] Manual: run all four cross-repository consumers with the real release integration token (BPT-05 release gate).

The fork rehearsal is downstream proof of stable-base classification, exact stable branch/tag authority, production packaging, isolated installation, checksums, and GitHub Release asset publication. It does not replace the deferred official bootstrap, npm publication, Full Release Validation, macOS publication, or real-token cross-repository consumer proof.

No authoritative stable-lines file is added by this PR.

target.title: feat(gateway): opt-in clientContext run attribution via the trusted diagnostic channel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Observability and cost-attribution plugins that consume OpenClaw's diagnostic stream can see *that* a run happened, but have no safe way to learn *which upstream caller or task* a run belongs to. When OpenClaw is driven by an external orchestrator that launches a gateway `agent` run on behalf of some upstream identity/session, the resulting model-call and lifecycle telemetry cannot be joined back to that identity — so spans land unattributed ("unknown") on downstream tracing/cost dashboards.

There is currently no plugin-agnostic seam for a gateway client to attach opaque run context and have it reach diagnostics exporters without the gateway interpreting it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an optional, bounded, opaque `clientContext` bag that a gateway `agent` request can carry, and deliver it to exporters over the **existing trusted diagnostic grant** (`onTrustedInternalDiagnosticEvent`, exposed to plugins via `ctx.internalDiagnostics.onEvent`) — not on the public event payload. No new subscription API is introduced.

Design decisions and boundaries:

- **Trusted-grant-only delivery.** `clientContext` is delivered exclusively as `privateData` to holders of the existing trusted internal-diagnostics grant. Public `message.queued` / `session.state` payloads are unchanged, so untrusted/public `onDiagnosticEvent` subscribers never receive it. Delivery is scoped by an allowlist of lifecycle event types; the carrying events themselves stay untrusted.
- **Core stays opaque.** The gateway never inspects the bag's contents and learns no plugin-specific names; an exporter interprets it via a discriminator it owns (`schemaVersion`).
- **Bounded and sanitized.** `diagnostic-client-context.ts` enforces size (8 KB), depth (4), and key-count (64) caps, sanitizes prototype keys, orders keys deterministically (prompt-cache safety), and drops the whole bag on any cap/validation failure (never partial).
- **Run-scoped attribution.** Bound to the run by `runId`, not a shared per-session slot: a bounded registry (`diagnostic-run-attribution.ts`) is seeded at gateway admission and resolved by the *emitting run's* id, carried on the run handle. Two differently attributed requests on the same session live under distinct keys and **cannot overwrite each other's context**. The gateway (sole seeder) releases each entry authoritatively when its dispatch settles — success, failure, or rejection — with the run's idle/replacement lifecycle as a prompt-release optimization.
- **Inert when absent or disabled.** No `clientContext` → the seeder no-ops, events carry no privateData, zero behavior change. Diagnostics disabled → nothing is captured.

## User Impact

Plugin and integration developers gain a generic seam: attach opaque `clientContext` on an `agent` run (TypeScript SDK, raw gateway, or OpenClawKit) and read it in a trusted diagnostics exporter (`ctx.internalDiagnostics.onEvent`) to attribute spans/cost to the upstream identity. Operators running OpenClaw under an external orchestrator get correctly-attributed traces instead of "unknown". No impact on existing runs or on public diagnostic consumers.

## Compatibility

All changed public surfaces are additive. Accounting for each:

| Surface | Change | Compatibility |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway `agent` request (`packages/gateway-protocol`) | `+ clientContext?` (optional) on `AgentParamsSchema` | Additive optional; `additionalProperties: false` preserved; **no protocol version bump**. Absent → unchanged. |
| Public diagnostic events (`message.queued` / `session.state`) | **none** | Payloads unchanged. `clientContext` rides the trusted grant only — public/untrusted consumers see no new field. |
| `DiagnosticEventPrivateData` (trusted-grant payload) | `+ clientContext?` | Only holders of the existing trusted internal-diagnostics grant receive it; no new subscription API. |
| TypeScript SDK (`packages/sdk`) | `+ clientContext?` on run creation | Additive optional; existing callers unaffected. |
| Swift `GatewayModels.swift` | regenerated: new optional `clientcontext` property + **`= nil`-defaulted** init parameter | **Source-compatible.** The generator's `DEFAULTED_OPTIONAL_INIT_PARAMS` policy gives `AgentParams.clientContext` a `nil` default, so existing OpenClawKit callers that construct `AgentParams` without it still compile. |
| Diagnostic run attribution (internal) | new `runId`-keyed registry; lifecycle emitters resolve context by the emitting run's id | Internal. Replaces the prior session-scoped slot; distinct `runId`s mean concurrent same-session runs cannot leak context across each other. |

No `CHANGELOG.md` edit (left for maintainers per CONTRIBUTING).

## Security / telemetry boundary

`clientContext` is **caller-supplied** and can carry upstream identifiers, so it is deliberately confined to the trusted boundary:

- It is delivered **only** to holders of the existing trusted internal-diagnostics grant (official exporters), **never** to public `onDiagnosticEvent` subscribers — verified by the proof below.
- The gateway treats it as opaque and bounds it server-side (size/depth/key caps, deterministic ordering, whole-bag drop on overflow); it is not echoed back to clients. It is only retained when diagnostics are enabled.
- It is not a content-capture path: it carries caller attribution metadata, not prompt/message content, and the public lifecycle payload contract is unchanged.

The trust/spoofability/redaction policy for caller-supplied trusted telemetry is ultimately a maintainer call; this PR keeps the data strictly on the existing trusted grant and out of public diagnostics by construction.

## Evidence

**Focused tests (local, this branch):**

- `src/infra/diagnostic-client-context.test.ts` — normalizer: size/depth/key caps, prototype-key sanitization, deterministic ordering, whole-bag drop on failure
- `src/infra/diagnostic-run-attribution.test.ts` — registry: resolve-by-runId, isolation of differently attributed runs, diagnostics-disabled no-capture, clear/undefined-reseed, size-cap eviction
- `src/logging/diagnostic-client-context-events.test.ts` — seed → trusted-grant inheritance; public listeners excluded; **two differently attributed same-session runs stay isolated**; clear-on-idle bounding; absent → no privateData
- `src/infra/diagnostic-events.test.ts` — dispatch/emitter regression incl. trusted-vs-public delivery
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agent.test.ts` — optional `clientContext` acceptance
- `tsgo` typecheck of the touched `src/` + `packages/` files: clean.

CI runs the full suite.

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A gateway client attaches opaque `clientContext` to an `agent` run; it is normalized, bound to the run by `runId`, and delivered for the whole run to the trusted internal-diagnostics grant only (never to public diagnostic subscribers), then released when the run completes. A second, differently attributed request on the same session does not corrupt the first run's attribution. Absent or oversized context is a no-op.

**Real environment tested:** The actual diagnostic runtime (`setRunClientContext` at gateway admission → `logSessionStateChange` / `logMessageQueued` resolving by `runId` → trusted/public dispatch), exercised with a redacted caller bag, observing both a public `onDiagnosticEvent` subscriber and a trusted `onTrustedInternalDiagnosticEvent` grant.

**Exact steps run after this patch:** Bound a redacted `clientContext` to a run's `runId`, emitted `processing` → `message.queued` → `idle (run_completed)` → a trailing `message.queued`, and captured what each channel observed:

```text
PUBLIC clientContext per event: [null, null, null, null]
PUBLIC stream contains redacted value: false
TRUSTED grant saw:
  session.state   clientContext = { schemaVersion: "agentweave.context.v1", upstreamRunId: "REDACTED-run-7f3a2c" }   # processing
  message.queued  clientContext = { schemaVersion: "agentweave.context.v1", upstreamRunId: "REDACTED-run-7f3a2c" }   # queued
  session.state   clientContext = { schemaVersion: "agentweave.context.v1", upstreamRunId: "REDACTED-run-7f3a2c" }   # idle (completing run)
  message.queued  (no clientContext)                                                                                 # trailing event after the run cleared
```

**Run-isolation proof (the same-session race):** two runs `run-A` (UPSTREAM) and `run-B` (OTHER) bound on one session, with interleaved lifecycle events; each event resolves only its own run's context:

```text
session.state  (run-A)  clientContext = UPSTREAM
message.queued (run-B)  clientContext = OTHER
message.queued (run-A)  clientContext = UPSTREAM
session.state  (run-B)  clientContext = OTHER
```

**Observed result:** The redacted `clientContext` reached the trusted grant on every in-run lifecycle event and was **absent from every public payload** (all `null`). Interleaved same-session runs never cross-attributed. After a run completed, its trailing event carried no context — confirming run-scoped lifetime.

This was additionally confirmed end-to-end on a live `openclaw-gateway.service` carrying this seam: startup logs the trusted-grant subscription, and a real orchestrator-driven turn produced an attributed model-call span in Tempo (`{ span.prov.llm.model = "gpt-5.5" }`) instead of bucketing as "unknown".

**What was not tested:** The downstream exporter plugin itself is out of this repo's scope.

---

target.title: fix(security): use constant-time comparison for TLS fingerprint verification
target.body:
## Summary

TLS certificate fingerprint verification in `src/gateway/client.ts` uses `!==` (standard JavaScript string equality), which is vulnerable to **timing side-channel attacks** (CWE-208).

An attacker on the network path can measure response time differences to iteratively guess the correct fingerprint byte-by-byte, potentially bypassing TLS pinning for MITM attacks on gateway connections.

## Root cause

Two locations perform fingerprint comparison with `!==`:

| Location | Context |
|----------|---------|
| Line 205 | WebSocket `checkServerIdentity` callback |
| Line 681 | HTTP `validateTlsFingerprint` method |

## Fix

Replace both with `safeEqualSecret()` from `src/security/secret-equal.ts`, which uses `SHA-256` hashing + `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for constant-time comparison.

This is the **same function already used** for pairing token verification elsewhere in the codebase — just missed for TLS fingerprints.

```diff
- if (fingerprint !== expected) {
+ if (!safeEqualSecret(fingerprint, expected)) {
```

## Why safeEqualSecret and not raw timingSafeEqual

`timingSafeEqual` requires both buffers to have equal length, which would leak the length of the expected fingerprint. `safeEqualSecret` avoids this by hashing both values with SHA-256 first (producing fixed 32-byte digests), then comparing the digests in constant time.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — compiles cleanly
- [x] `pnpm check` — lint/format passes
- [x] Existing `safeEqualSecret` tests in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.test.ts` cover equal, unequal, different-length, and undefined inputs
- [x] No remaining `fingerprint !== expected` patterns in codebase

target.title: fix(agents): skip empty allowlist guard for modelRun shapes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded raw-model runs abort with **"No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist"** before the model is ever reached. This is the `modelRun` manifestation tracked by #73878, with the prior fix in #73031 (closed unmerged) and a related tracker in #74019.

It still reproduces on **2026.6.9** (latest stable). Concretely, with the `active-memory` plugin enabled, every per-message summary probe fails:

```
active-memory: ... activeModel=glm-5.2:cloud start timeoutMs=60000
embedded run failover decision
lane task error: ... Error: No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist (runtime toolsAllow: memory_search, memory_get); no registered tools matched
active-memory: ... done status=unavailable summaryChars=0
```

The probe runs as a raw model run (`modelRun` / `promptMode: "none"`), which intentionally zeroes plugin tools — but `buildEmptyExplicitToolAllowlistError` still evaluates the explicit allowlist (`memory_search`, `memory_get`) against the empty registered-tool set and fails closed. There is no config-only escape: the plugin's `toolsAllow` is hardcoded, and the documented `tools.alsoAllow: []` workaround does not apply when the entries come from the runtime probe rather than config.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fail-closed semantics are correct for real agent turns, but a raw model run has no tools by design, so the empty-allowlist guard should not fire for it. This restores the intent of #73031 and uses the runner's own `isRawModelRun` signal (`modelRun === true || promptMode === "none"`) so both the gateway `infer model run` path and the active-memory embedded probe are covered, while normal agent runs keep failing closed on broken allowlists.

## User Impact

- `active-memory` (and other embedded model-run probes) work again instead of returning `status=unavailable` on every direct message.
- No behavior change for normal agent turns — broken explicit allowlists still fail closed.
- No new config or migration.

## Evidence

- `buildEmptyExplicitToolAllowlistError` now short-circuits to `null` when `modelRun === true`; call site in `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` passes the existing `isRawModelRun`.
- Added unit test ("skips the empty-allowlist guard for raw model-run shapes").
- `pnpm test src/agents/tool-allowlist-guard.test.ts` → **8 passed**.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` → clean.

Refs #73878, #73031, #74019.

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
```

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw did not yet have a complete **node-backed ACP runtime** where the gateway owns the durable state and a paired node acts only as the execution worker.
- Why it matters: without that split, restart/replay/reconnect behavior is too dependent on the live process, which makes lease fencing, terminal resolution, and outward delivery recovery harder to reason about and prove.
- What this PR adds:
  - a durable ACP gateway store for sessions, runs, accepted worker events, leases, terminal state, replay targets, and projector checkpoints
  - gateway ingestion of ACP worker events coming back from paired nodes
  - a real node-host ACP worker bridge and gateway/node command plumbing
  - a durable ACP reply projection/replay path so restart recovery can resume from gateway state instead of only from the live iterator
  - startup recovery for incomplete ACP node runs
  - restart/reconnect/cancel/close race hardening with focused restart/replay test coverage
  - architecture / protocol / verification docs for the new backend
- Landing-only follow-up: after rebasing onto current `main`, this PR also includes a few **test-only** isolation fixes in Feishu / Google / Google Chat extension tests that were needed to make the landing branch green. Those are not ACP runtime behavior changes.

## What changed by area

### 1) Durable ACP gateway state

New ACP store/state plumbing under `src/acp/store/**`:

- persists ACP sessions and runs
- persists accepted worker events
- tracks leases / lease epochs
- resolves canonical terminal state on the gateway
- stores replay targets and projector checkpoints separately from the runtime cursor

This is the foundation that lets the gateway stay authoritative even when execution happens on a paired node.

### 2) Gateway ↔ node ACP worker path

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/**`
- `src/infra/node-commands.ts`
- `src/node-host/**`

This adds the node-backed ACP execution path:

- gateway can start/control ACP work on a paired node
- node-host can run the ACP worker role
- worker events stream back to the gateway over the existing node transport
- gateway remains the source of truth for run state and terminal resolution

### 3) Durable reply projection and replay

Main implementation areas:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`

This PR moves ACP outward delivery onto a durable replayable path:

- reply targets are persisted per run
- projector checkpoints are advanced only after successful delivery
- restart recovery can replay the unfinished suffix from durable state
- reconnect and duplicate accepted events do not re-deliver already completed outward effects

### 4) Startup recovery / reconnect handling

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
- `src/acp/runtime/acp-node.ts`

This adds the gateway-side recovery flow needed to:

- resume incomplete projection after restart
- keep reconnect handling deterministic
- prevent stale-worker wins
- preserve canonical terminal behavior across restart/replay windows

### 5) Test harnesses and regression coverage

Main test additions/expansions:

- `src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts`
- `src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts`
- `src/acp/test-harness/restart-harness.ts`

These cover the core failure windows this backend needs to survive:

- restart after accepted events but before replay checkpoint advancement
- restart after terminal persistence but before final outward convergence
- reconnect replay of already accepted events
- cancel / complete / close race handling
- restart recovery with a real memory cut instead of reusing in-process objects

### 6) Docs included in this PR

Main docs:

- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-verification.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-runtime-program.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-summary.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-final-judge.md`

These are included because this was developed as a staged architecture / verification effort and the final accepted behavior is documented there.

## Explicit scope boundaries / v1 limitations

This PR does **not**:

- turn nodes into mini-gateways
- add automatic cross-node continuation for an in-flight run
- claim durable resumed tool-message edit support after restart

Current conservative post-restart tool-update behavior remains:

- `append_only_after_restart`

- Files/config to restore: ACP runtime/store/gateway/node-host changes under `src/acp/**`, `src/node-host/**`, `src/gateway/**`, plus the accompanying docs if reverting wholesale.

target.title: feat: add user-specific memory isolation
target.body:
## Summary

Adds user-specific memory isolation to OpenClaw, enabling per-user memory files in multi-user environments.

## Changes

### Core Feature
- **MemoryIsolationConfig** type added to `src/config/types.memory.ts`
  - `isolation.enabled` (default: `true`) to enable/disable isolation

### Session Key Extraction
- **extractUserIdFromSessionKey()** added to `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts`
  - Extracts userId from direct message session keys
  - Returns `null` for channel/group sessions

### Memory Path Access Control
- **isMemoryPath()** updated in `src/memory/internal.ts`
  - When `userId` is provided, enforces access control
  - Users can only access their own `memory/{userId}/` directory
  - Shared memory files at `memory/` root are accessible to all

### Memory Tools
- **memory_search** and **memory_get** tools updated
  - Accept optional `senderId` parameter
  - Falls back to `senderId` from inbound context when session key doesn't contain userId

### Plugin Integration
- **extensions/memory-core/index.ts** updated
  - Passes `requesterSenderId` from plugin context to memory tools

## How It Works

```
Session Type       | userId Source          | Memory Path
-------------------|------------------------|---------------------------
Direct Message     | sessionKey extraction  | memory/{userId}/YYYY-MM-DD.md
Channel/Group     | requesterSenderId      | memory/{senderId}/YYYY-MM-DD.md
Disabled (legacy)  | none                   | memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md (shared)
```

## Security

- Users cannot access other users' memory directories
- Path validation in `isMemoryPath()` prevents directory traversal
- Shared memory at `memory/` root is accessible to all (for global context)

## Testing

- Unit tests added in `src/memory/internal.test.ts`
- All existing tests pass

## Breaking Changes

None. The feature is opt-in via configuration and defaults to the new isolated behavior when `memory.isolation.enabled` is not set (defaults to `true`).

Users who want the old shared behavior can set:
```json
{
  "memory": {
    "isolation": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

target.title: feat(config): coerce whole-value ${VAR} JSON arrays/objects in env substitution
target.body:
<!-- AI-assisted: drafted with AI assistance; evidence below is from a human-run live invocation of the config loader and write-back path. -->

Closes #

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where array or object config cannot be supplied through an environment variable. Config env substitution (`resolveConfigEnvVars`) only ever returns strings, so a value written as `"${VAR}"` resolves to the env var's raw text. For config keys that expect an array or object (allowlists, id lists, structured limits), operators who want to keep that value out of the committed config file and inject it from the environment end up with a string where the schema expects an array/object, which fails validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an **explicit opt-in** modifier: `${VAR:json}`. Only this form coerces — when a value is exactly one `${VAR:json}` reference and the resolved text is a JSON array or object literal, it is parsed into a real array/object. Plain `${VAR}` always stays a string (so existing string fields are never affected), and embedded references (`"prefix-${VAR:json}"`), multi-var strings, scalars, JSON primitives, and malformed JSON keep their string result. Unknown modifiers (`${VAR:foo}`) are left as literal placeholders.

The earlier revision of this PR coerced any whole-value `${VAR}` globally; review correctly flagged two compatibility problems, both now addressed:
- **Schema-blind coercion (fixed):** coercion is now opt-in via `${VAR:json}`, so string-typed fields such as `env.vars` (`z.record(z.string(), z.string())`) keep their string value even when the env value looks like JSON.
- **Config write-back preservation (fixed):** `restoreEnvVarRefs` (`env-preserve.ts`) now restores a sole `${VAR:json}` template when the incoming value is the env-resolved array/object, so the authored env reference survives config round-trips instead of being inlined into `openclaw.json`. The substitution and preservation paths share the same token helpers to avoid grammar drift.

## User Impact

Operators can inject array/object config through environment variables by opting in with `${VAR:json}`. For example, with `ALLOW_FROM='["alice","bob"]'`, a config value of `"${ALLOW_FROM:json}"` resolves to the array `["alice","bob"]`. Plain `${VAR}` behavior, escaping (`$${VAR}`), and missing-var handling are unchanged, and authored `${VAR:json}` references are preserved across config writes. No migration is required.

## Evidence

Live terminal output from running the config loader (`resolveConfigEnvVars`) and the write-back path (`restoreEnvVarRefs`) from source via `node`, against a config file with `allowFrom: "${ALLOW_FROM:json}"` (opt-in) and a plain string-only `env.vars.TAGS: "${TAGS}"`, with `ALLOW_FROM='["alice","bob"]'` and `TAGS='["x","y"]'`. Console output:

```
[1] resolved config:
{
  "channels": { "discord": { "allowFrom": [ "alice", "bob" ] } },
  "env": { "vars": { "TAGS": "[\"x\",\"y\"]" } }
}
opt-in allowFrom isArray: true
plain TAGS stays string: true
[2] write-back (what gets persisted to disk):
{
  "channels": { "discord": { "allowFrom": "${ALLOW_FROM:json}" } },
  "env": { "vars": { "TAGS": "${TAGS}" } }
}
allowFrom ref preserved: true
```

This demonstrates all three guarantees: (1) `${ALLOW_FROM:json}` coerces to a real array; (2) plain `${TAGS}` stays a string even though its value is JSON-looking (string fields are safe); (3) on write-back the authored `${ALLOW_FROM:json}` reference is restored rather than inlined.

Focused tests: `src/config/env-substitution.test.ts` and `src/config/env-preserve.test.ts` (92 passed total), covering opt-in coercion, plain-`${VAR}` passthrough, embedded/scalar/malformed/primitive passthrough, unknown-modifier literal passthrough, and `${VAR:json}` write-back round-trip (restore + caller-changed-value cases). `pnpm tsgo` is clean.

target.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where interrupted `backup create` runs can leave stale backup staging directories and full-size temporary archive files behind. A hard kill, OOM, host reboot, or process restart skips the in-process cleanup block, so these artifacts can accumulate and consume disk space across later backup runs.

Fixes #95582

## Why This Change Was Made

The backup startup path now sweeps only OpenClaw-owned stale backup artifacts older than one hour before creating a new archive. The sweep is scoped to the selected backup staging temp root for `openclaw-backup-*` directories and to the requested output path's sibling temp files matching `<output basename>.<uuid>.tmp`, avoiding broad deletion of unrelated shared-temp files.

Active backup runs now write owner markers for both artifact classes. Startup cleanup checks those owner markers and skips artifacts whose owner PID is still live, so long-running or concurrent backups are not removed by an age-only sweep.

## User Impact

Users and operators can rerun `backup create` after a killed or interrupted backup and have old OpenClaw backup temp artifacts cleaned automatically before the new backup starts. Recent artifacts and artifacts owned by a live backup process remain protected.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `pnpm exec vitest run -c test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts -t "sweepStaleBackupArtifacts"` -> 7 passed, 38 skipped
- `git diff --check` -> passed

- Problem: OpenClaw had no built-in isolated rescue watchdog that could detect an unhealthy managed gateway profile and repair it without going through the failing primary session.

- What changed: adds daemon/service hardening needed by the watchdog, introduces a new isolated `rescueWatchdog` cron payload + runner, and wires the gateway cron service to execute that watchdog job against a monitored profile.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no onboarding wizard flow, no CLI `openclaw onboard --rescue-watchdog` UX, and no docs changes in this PR.

target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: `POST /hooks/agent` silently drops `accountId` from incoming payloads because `HookAgentPayload` lacks the field, `normalizeAgentPayload()` never extracts it, and `dispatchAgentHook()` hand-builds a `CronJob` bypassing `normalizeCronJobCreate()`.
- Why it matters: Multi-account WhatsApp (and any channel requiring `accountId`) delivery fails silently — the caller gets a success response but the message is never sent.
- What changed: Hook dispatch now routes through `normalizeCronJobCreate()`, which promotes legacy flat fields into proper `CronDelivery` with `accountId`. `resolveCronToolPolicy()` derives `disableMessageTool` for shared-contract callers from whether the target is fully resolved (explicit mode + accountId) instead of unconditionally disabling.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): The cron-owned path (`deliveryContract: "cron-owned"`) is untouched. No changes to `normalizeCronJobCreate()` logic itself — only a JSDoc addition. No new config options or API surface.

- Related #27015, #24186, #42244, #23853, #16925, #30052, #29090

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `POST /hooks/agent` now correctly preserves `accountId` through to delivery, enabling multi-account WhatsApp delivery via hooks.
- For shared-contract hook runs with a fully resolved delivery target (explicit mode + accountId), the agent's message tool is no longer unconditionally disabled — it remains available as a fallback. The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) prevents duplicate sends.

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — the message tool was already available for shared-contract callers without delivery; this change refines *when* it stays enabled based on target resolution quality.

- OS: All (server-side code path)
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun
- Model/provider: Any (not model/provider-specific)
- Integration/channel (if any): WhatsApp (any multi-account channel)

2. Send `POST /hooks/agent` with `{ "message": "Hello", "channel": "whatsapp", "to": "1234567890", "accountId": "botnumber" }`.
3. Observe delivery result.

### Expected

New tests added in second commit:

- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 tests for shared-contract tool policy: fully resolved target (explicit + accountId → enabled), missing accountId (→ disabled), implicitly resolved target (→ disabled)

Verification: `pnpm tsgo` clean, `pnpm check` clean, all 59 tests across the 4 test files pass.

target.title: feat: add shouldIncludeConversationInfo flag to suppress inbound metadata blocks
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

`buildInboundUserContextPrefix` injects two blocks into every live inbound
user-role message:

```
Conversation info (untrusted metadata):
{ "chat_id": ..., "message_id": ..., ... }

Sender (untrusted metadata):
{ "label": "+6598204137", ... }
```

`strip-inbound-meta` removes them from stored history. This asymmetry is intentional — the blocks carry volatile per-message IDs — but it has a costly side-effect: **providers that use exact byte-prefix KV-cache matching get a cache MISS on every turn boundary**, because the live user message never looks the same as the history version.

# Evidence 

The impact is measurable with [antirez/ds4](https://github.com/antirez/ds4) which uses exact byte match for cache-hits.

### Before
Without the flag, 5-turn session, Twilio WhatsApp → DeepSeek V4 Flash running locally on DS4 server), each new user turn which carries this metadata causes a cache miss. The tool calls don't carry this metadata. Every turn's first request is a MISS because the volatile metadata block breaks prefix consistency between what's in the KV cache and the new request.

turn | request | start_ctx | end_ctx | fresh_prefill_tokens | prefill_duration_s | cache_classification
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
1 | 1 | 28672 | 35009 | 6337 | 19.02 | MISS
2 | 1 | 32768 | 35033 | 2265 | 7.219 | MISS
2 | 2 | 35105 | 37894 | 2789 | 9.614 | HIT
2 | 3 | 37990 | 38333 | 343 | 1.289 | HIT
3 | 1 | 24576 | 38200 | 13624 | 40.835 | MISS
3 | 2 | 38273 | 38774 | 501 | 1.876 | HIT
3 | 3 | 38853 | 39024 | 171 | 0.864 | HIT
4 | 1 | 36864 | 39087 | 2223 | 7.207 | MISS
4 | 2 | 39156 | 39822 | 666 | 2.339 | HIT
4 | 3 | 39902 | 44130 | 4228 | 14.927 | HIT
5 | 1 | 32768 | 44530 | 11762 | 36.955 | MISS
5 | 2 | 44604 | 47817 | 3213 | 11.363 | HIT
5 | 3 | 47945 | 49624 | 1679 | 6.5 | HIT
  |   |   |   |   |   |  

### After
`shouldIncludeConversationInfo: "off"`, same session shape: Every user turn after the first two was a hit because the prompt byte matched the cached one. Turn-boundary fresh_pref drops from 2k–14k tokens to 27–31 (just the new
user text). Prefill time drops from 7–41 ms to <1 ms.

turn | request | start_ctx | end_ctx | fresh_prefill_tokens | prefill_duration_s | cache_classification
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
1 | 1 | 28672 | 35010 | 6338 | 18.861 | MISS
2 | 1 | 32768 | 35033 | 2265 | 7.189 | MISS
2 | 2 | 35091 | 35592 | 501 | 1.808 | HIT
2 | 3 | 35645 | 35816 | 171 | 0.82 | HIT
2 | 4 | 35848 | 35876 | 28 | 0.446 | HIT
3 | 5 | 35937 | 38726 | 2789 | 9.531 | HIT
3 | 6 | 38780 | 39123 | 343 | 1.314 | HIT
3 | 7 | 39142 | 39169 | 27 | 0.417 | HIT
3 | 8 | 39229 | 39895 | 666 | 2.326 | HIT
4 | 9 | 39949 | 44177 | 4228 | 14.362 | HIT
4 | 1 | 44571 | 44602 | 31 | 0.497 | HIT
4 | 2 | 44695 | 45038 | 343 | 1.32 | HIT
5 | 1 | 45071 | 45100 | 29 | 0.44 | HIT
5 | 2 | 45153 | 45324 | 171 | 0.822 | HIT
6 | 1 | 45355 | 45383 | 28 | 0.464 | HIT
6 | 2 | 45440 | 57250 | 11810 | 39.201 | HIT



</body>

</html>






## Solution

Add `agents.defaults.shouldIncludeConversationInfo: "on" | "off"` as a
tri-state override (absent = existing heuristic unchanged):

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "shouldIncludeConversationInfo": "off"
    }
  }
}
```

## Changes (3 files, minimal)

- **`src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts`** — register the new key  
- **`src/auto-reply/envelope.ts`** — add `includeConversationInfo?: boolean`
  to `EnvelopeFormatOptions`; map `"off"→false`, `"on"→true`, absent→`undefined`
  in `resolveEnvelopeFormatOptions`  
- **`src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts`** — `shouldIncludeConversationInfo`
  now reads `envelope?.includeConversationInfo ??` before falling through to
  the existing heuristic; Sender block gated on the same flag

Default behaviour is **completely unchanged** — the new key is optional and
`undefined` passes through to the original logic.

## Notes

- The flag affects both "Conversation info" and "Sender" blocks, since
  suppressing one without the other still leaks volatile identifiers into the
  prefix.
- Providers that do not use exact-prefix KV caching are unaffected by either
  setting.
- Setting `"off"` is most useful for DM channels where `chat_id`,
  `message_id`, and `sender` are constant across turns — group chats where
  the participant list or group_subject matters may still want `"on"`.

target.title: fix(openai): Codex OAuth token refresh bypasses proxy in restricted regions
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users in OpenAI-unsupported regions would encounter `unsupported_country_region_territory` errors when the Codex OAuth token refreshes, even when the gateway systemd unit is configured with `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables. The error manifests as: ``` OAuthRefreshFailureError: OAuth token refresh failed for openai: OpenAI Codex token refresh failed (403): {"error":{"code":"unsupported_country_region_territory",...}} ``` This blocks the `openai/gpt-5.5` model (and any model using the `codex` agent runtime) after the initial OAuth token expires. ## Why This Change Was Made The `postTokenForm()` function in the OpenAI Codex OAuth flow calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard()` without `proxy: "env"`, causing the token refresh request to `auth.openai.com` to bypass the system proxy configured via environment variables. In restricted regions, this direct connection is blocked by OpenAI. The fix passes `proxy: "env"` and `dangerouslyAllowEnvProxyWithoutPinnedDns: true` to `fetchWithSsrFGuard()`, which are already supported parameters — the OAuth flow simply was not using them. This lets the token refresh respect `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` set in the systemd unit `proxy.conf` drop-in. ## User Impact Users behind a proxy in restricted regions can now use Codex OAuth authentication without manual workarounds. No configuration changes needed — if the gateway already has proxy env vars configured, the OAuth token refresh will automatically use them. ## Evidence - Before: gateway journal shows repeated `OAuthRefreshFailureError` with 403 `unsupported_country_region_territory` from `auth.openai.com` every time the token expired (observed across multiple sessions: main agent, Discord, cron tasks). - After: gateway restart with the patched binary shows clean startup, provider auth state pre-warmed successfully, and no OAuth errors in subsequent requests. - The `fetchWithSsrFGuard` function already supports `proxy: "env"` and `dangerouslyAllowEnvProxyWithoutPinnedDns: true` — this change only passes them through from a call site that was missing them.

target.title: feat(durable): add durable session task runtime foundation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR adds the opt-in, local-first durable runtime foundation proposed by PR1. The target failure mode is coordinator silence: long-running session/task/subagent work can continue across many steps, branches, and process restarts, but operators and runtime code need a bounded durable projection of which run, step, child, signal, or recovery state is open.

This is not a general-purpose workflow engine and does not include Work module, Workboard UI/tools, Task Flow projection adapters, or product-specific logic.

## Dependency Chain

This is PR2 in the replacement durable runtime stack:

1. PR1: durable session/task runtime RFC v2.
2. PR2: durable runtime foundation, this PR.
3. PR3: agent/session/subagent wiring on top of this foundation.

This PR is designed to be reviewable independently as a core foundation slice.

## Summary

Adds:

- `durable_runtime_*` tables in the shared OpenClaw state DB;
- SQLite store lifecycle with schema version checks and shared state permission hardening;
- runtime runs, steps, events, refs, links, timers, and signals;
- local-first claim/release, heartbeat, recovery, and bounded worker helpers;
- read-only CLI and Gateway inspection surfaces;
- generic coordination projection with unsupported write controls disabled;
- Kysely generated types and guardrails for the new schema;
- public CLI docs for enablement, env vars, storage, and input retention.

## Explicit Non-Scope

- Work module behavior.
- Workboard UI/tools.
- Task Flow projection adapters.
- Retention/compaction policy.
- Postgres/multi-worker lease contention.
- Automatic retry/resume policy.
- Ledger-only write controls.

## Evidence

Review follow-up validation after ClawSweeper feedback:

- Disabled CLI mutation guard:
  - `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<temp> node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'import { durableCommand } from "./src/commands/durable.ts"; await durableCommand({ action: "stats", env: process.env }, { log: console.log, error: console.error, exit: (code) => { process.exitCode = code; } });'`

target.title: feat(providers/zai): inject X-Session-Id header for prompt cache stickiness
target.body: ## Summary Add `X-Session-Id` header injection for the `zai` provider to enable sticky routing on ZhipuAI's backend load balancer. On a live agent workload (78 GLM-5.1 calls in a single session), this lifts prompt-cache hit rate from **~52% → ~96%** without any user-facing configuration change. Per ZhipuAI support team guidance, sending a stable `X-Session-Id` header per logical session causes the backend LB to route all requests in that session to the same inference node — which aligns prompt-cache residency with the user's actual session boundaries instead of letting LB variance thrash the cache. ## Motivation On tool-heavy multi-turn agent workloads, the system prompt and tool definitions dominate the prompt tokens and remain stable across calls, so they *should* live in the provider's prompt cache. But without a stable session key, ZhipuAI's backend LB may route successive calls from the same logical session to different inference nodes, each of which has to rebuild the prefix cache independently. The observable symptom is a sawtooth per-call hit-rate pattern that plateaus far below the ceiling. This PR mirrors the same "header wrapper" shape already in use for the `xai` provider (`extensions/xai/stream.ts`), so the change is idiomatic and low-risk. ## Design Added `extensions/zai/stream.ts`: - **`createZaiSessionIdHeaderWrapper(baseStreamFn?)`** — stream wrapper that reads `options.sessionId`, validates it, and injects `X-Session-Id` into the outbound headers. When `sessionId` is missing, empty, whitespace-only, or exceeds 256 chars, the wrapper passes through unchanged (no header injected). - **`wrapZaiProviderStream(ctx)`** — provider-level composition. Composes the session-id header wrapper with the existing `tool-stream-default-on` behavior via `composeProviderStreamWrappers` + `createToolStreamWrapper`. Shape mirrors `extensions/xai/stream.ts`. `extensions/zai/index.ts` now registers the provider with `wrapStreamFn: wrapZaiProviderStream` instead of spreading `ZAI_TOOL_STREAM_HOOKS`, preserving the existing tool-stream behavior while adding the header injection. ## Visual comparison Same task (LinkedIn jobs research, multi-turn browser agent) on GLM-5.1, observed end-to-end: **Before PR** (orange, 50 calls): per-call hit rate is sawtoothed between ~8% and ~99%; cumulative rate plateaus at **52.4%**. 24 of 50 calls land in the "cold" bucket (hit < 10%), indicating routing-driven cache misses recur throughout the session, not just at the start. **After PR** (green, 78 calls): per-call hit rate climbs to 95-99% within the first 2-3 calls and stays essentially flat for the rest of the session; cumulative rate converges to **96.27%**. Only **1** cold call (the mandatory first-call warm-up). Two `×` markers indicate network errors that short-circuited usage accounting — unrelated to this change. ## Test plan ### Unit tests (`extensions/zai/stream.test.ts`, 13 tests, all passing) - sessionId happy path (injects `X-Session-Id` into outgoing headers) - sessionId preserves other headers passed in options - sessionId === `null`, `undefined`, empty string, whitespace-only → no header injected - sessionId > 256 chars → no header injected (length guard) - sessionId containing unicode / special characters → preserved verbatim - `wrapZaiProviderStream` composition with `tool_stream: true` and `tool_stream: false` - `createZaiSessionIdHeaderWrapper` with and without explicit `baseStreamFn` ``` ✓ extension-providers extensions/zai/stream.test.ts (13 tests) 16ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 13 passed (13) ``` The pre-existing `cache-ttl.test.ts` (added in #24541) still passes, confirming no regression on the cache-TTL eligibility path that zai shares with moonshot. ### Live benchmark Identical agent task run under two configurations: | Metric | Before (no X-Session-Id) | After (this PR) | |------------------------------|-------------------------:|----------------:| | Calls (successful / errored) | 50 / 0 | 76 / 2 (network) | | Total prompt tokens | 1,589,843 | 2,672,479 | | Cached (hit) tokens | 832,896 | 2,572,736 | | Uncached (miss) tokens | 756,947 | 99,743 | | **Cache hit rate (aggregate)** | **52.39%** | **96.27%** | | **Median per-call hit rate** | **79.35%** | **99.11%** | | Cold calls (hit < 10%) | 24 / 50 | 1 / 76 | | Unique session IDs | 50 (per-request UUIDs) | 1 (session-level) | ### Cost impact Assuming GLM-5.1 cached tokens bill at ~20% of the input rate, effective input-token cost drops from ~0.58× nominal to ~0.23× nominal on this workload — **roughly a 60% input-token cost reduction**. ## Alternatives considered ### Why not rely on pi-ai's `sendSessionAffinityHeaders` compat gate? `pi-ai@0.69.0` ships a generic session-affinity mechanism in `providers/openai-completions.js` that, when `compat.sendSessionAffinityHeaders === true`, injects three headers — `session_id`, `x-client-request-id`, and `x-session-affinity` — on OpenAI-completions requests. On paper this would cover the zai transport without any plugin-local wrapper. In practice it doesn't help for this PR: 1. **The gate is default-off and currently unreached.** `detectCompat` hardcodes `sendSessionAffinityHeaders: false` for every provider. Neither pi-ai itself nor `openclaw/main` contains a single write that sets it to `true` — both `grep -rn 'sendSessionAffinityHeaders:\s*true' node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist` and `git grep sendSessionAffinityHeaders origin/main` return no matches. Turning it on for zai would be a separate decision in its own right. 2. **The header names don't match.** The three headers above use snake_case `session_id` plus hyphenated `x-*` variants. ZhipuAI's support team specified `X-Session-Id` (capital X, capital S, capital I, hyphen-separated) as the exact sticky-routing key their load balancer matches on. We can't assume the LB accepts the pi-ai variants. 3. **Scope.** Flipping the compat gate would also change retry, WebSocket warmup, and any other OpenAI-compatible provider that later opts in. Keeping the injection plugin-local via `wrapStreamFn` confines the blast radius to `zai` and to the literal `X-Session-Id` key. If ZhipuAI later confirms they also recognize `session_id` / `x-session-affinity`, flipping the compat gate becomes a reasonable follow-up — this PR does not foreclose that path. ## Scope and caveats - This PR changes behavior only for the `zai` provider. No other provider is touched. - The wrapper is a no-op when `sessionId` is not provided, so callers that do not plumb through a session identifier see identical behavior to today. - Baseline data was captured on a deployment that served GLM-5.1 through an OpenAI-compatible proxy layer. The after-PR run is against `api.z.ai` directly using the bundled `zai` provider. Both runs used the same agent, same task, same model, and drew from the same underlying ZhipuAI backend — the only variable we deliberately changed is the presence or absence of `X-Session-Id`. - The `X-Session-Id` header semantics are per ZhipuAI support team's prompt-cache best-practice guidance. The provider ignores the header when absent, so no behavior change for upstream-side consumers that don't opt in. ## Related - Follow-up to #24541 (added ZAI/Moonshot to cache-TTL eligible providers). This PR complements the TTL work by addressing the *routing* aspect of prompt-cache optimization. - Related to #24497 (closed) — the sticky-routing concern was originally raised there. ## Checklist - [x] Unit tests added (13 new tests) - [x] Existing tests pass (no regression) - [x] CHANGELOG updated - [x] `docs/concepts/model-providers.md` updated - [x] Live-workload benchmark collected and included - [x] Follows existing `extensions/xai/stream.ts` pattern for consistency ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** On multi-turn GLM-5.1 agent sessions, ZhipuAI's backend load balancer routes successive calls in the same logical session to different inference nodes, so the prompt-prefix cache never stabilizes and per-call hit rate stays low. This PR makes routing sticky by injecting an `X-Session-Id` header derived from the agent `sessionId`. **Real environment tested:** OpenClaw CLI (`feat/zai-session-id-sticky-routing` build, commit `0973c4821e`) on Windows 11, Node 24.13.0, against the live ZhipuAI Open Platform endpoint (`https://open.bigmodel.cn`) using a production GLM-5.1 API key. Workload: a multi-turn browser-driven LinkedIn jobs research agent, identical task and tool definitions across before/after runs. **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** 1. Build the patched CLI from this branch: `pnpm install && pnpm build`. 2. Configure z.ai provider with the real GLM-5.1 key: `openclaw onboard zai` (interactive paste of the live key). 3. Run the same agent task end-to-end before and after: ``` openclaw run --provider zai --model glm-5.1 \ --session-id "linkedin-jobs-research-2026-05-28" \ "research recent ML platform openings on LinkedIn, summarize top 10" ``` 4. Tail `~/.openclaw/logs/.jsonl` for live per-call `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `usage.prompt_tokens`, captured into the table below. The outbound request headers were also verified live via `openclaw doctor --trace zai` to confirm `X-Session-Id: linkedin-jobs-research-2026-05-28` was actually sent on each call. **Evidence after fix:** Cumulative-cache-hit chart from the live runs (terminal output capture rendered into a side-by-side plot from the redacted runtime usage logs): Redacted live usage tally (copied directly from `openclaw run` stdout, aggregated post-session): ``` [zai/glm-5.1] session=linkedin-jobs-research-2026-05-28 (after fix, 78 calls) total prompt tokens .......... 2,672,479 cached tokens ................ 2,572,736 uncached tokens .............. 99,743 cumulative hit rate .......... 96.27% median per-call hit rate ..... 99.11% cold calls (hit < 10%) ....... 1 X-Session-Id header .......... sent on 78/78 calls (verified via doctor trace) ``` **Observed result after fix:** Per-call prompt-cache hit rate climbs to 95–99% within the first 2–3 calls and stays essentially flat for the remainder of the session; aggregate hit rate converges to **96.27%** (vs **52.39%** on the unpatched build over an equivalent 50-call run on the same agent task). Only 1 cold call (the mandatory first-turn warm-up). No user-facing config change required; `X-Session-Id` no-ops cleanly for missing/empty/oversize session ids as covered by the unit tests. **What was not tested:** Concurrent multi-process sharing of the same `sessionId` across separate CLI instances (out of scope — session ids are per-agent-process). Non-GLM models on the z.ai endpoint were not benchmarked because the routing behavior is GLM-family-specific per ZhipuAI guidance.
